Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-formaction

### A052 formenctype definition

`formenctype`. Override the submission encoding for the activated applicable submitter.

Watch for: The override must be paired with a method and endpoint that can handle it.

Context: button; input. Value grammar: "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"; "multipart/form-data"; "text/plain".

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-formenctype

### A053 formmethod definition

`formmethod`. Override the form's get, post or dialog method through the applicable submitter.

Watch for: Dialog closes the dialog workflow rather than sending an ordinary network request.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-formmethod

### A054 formnovalidate definition

`formnovalidate`. Bypass interactive constraint validation for the applicable submitter. It is boolean.

Watch for: It never exempts the server from validating received data.

Context: button; input. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-formnovalidate

### A055 formtarget definition

`formtarget`. Override the navigation target for the applicable submission.

Watch for: Named contexts and special keywords are navigation choices, not authorization.

### A056 headers definition

`headers`. List the IDs of related th cells for a td or th.

Watch for: Each reference must identify the intended header in the table; arbitrary IDs do not define useful associations.

Context: td; th. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens consisting of IDs*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#attr-tdth-headers

### A057 headingoffset definition

`headingoffset`. Apply a numeric offset to descendant heading levels under the current heading-level rules; allowed values are 0 through 8.

Watch for: This is a newer standard feature; keep explicit meaningful heading ranks and test accessibility mappings before relying on it.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Valid non-negative integer between 0 and 8.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#attr-headingoffset

### A058 headingreset definition

`headingreset`. Stop heading-offset computation from continuing beyond the marked element. It is a boolean boundary.

Watch for: This does not rewrite heading tag names or establish tested browser support.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#attr-headingreset

### A059 height definition

`height`. Set a vertical dimension on the eligible element. Canvas uses a backing-store coordinate dimension; image and video dimensions can reserve an aspect ratio.

Watch for: CSS display size and the underlying resource or bitmap size are different concepts.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#attr-canvas-height

### A060 hidden definition

`hidden`. Mark content as currently irrelevant to presentation. hidden or empty represents the ordinary hidden state; until-found supports a distinct reveal workflow.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#attr-hidden

### A061 high definition

`high`. On meter, set the beginning of the high-value subrange within the effective range.

Watch for: Thresholds must make sense alongside low, min, max and optimum.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-meter-high

### A062 href definition

`href`. Set a hyperlink destination on a or area, an external resource address on link, or the document base on base.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#attr-hyperlink-href

Context: link. Value grammar: Valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-href

Context: base. Value grammar: Valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-base-href

### A063 hreflang definition

`hreflang`. Hint the linked resource's human language using a valid language tag.

Watch for: It does not change this document's language or translate the destination.

Context: a; link. Value grammar: Valid BCP 47 language tag.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#attr-hyperlink-hreflang

### A064 http-equiv definition

`http-equiv`. Select a supported meta pragma, such as content-security-policy or refresh.

Watch for: It is not a universal way to set arbitrary HTTP response headers; several policies require real headers.

Context: meta. Value grammar: "content-type"; "default-style"; "refresh"; "x-ua-compatible"; "content-security-policy".

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-meta-http-equiv

### A065 id definition

`id`. Give an element a unique nonempty identifier without ASCII whitespace in its tree. IDs support fragments, labels, scripts and ID references.

Watch for: Duplicates can silently redirect associations; window named properties are not a safe lookup strategy.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Text*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#the-id-attribute

### A066 imagesizes definition

`imagesizes`. Describe source sizes for an image preload link using source-size syntax.

Watch for: Match the later responsive image's selection context to avoid unnecessary downloads.

Context: link. Value grammar: Valid source size list.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-imagesizes

### A067 imagesrcset definition

`imagesrcset`. Offer image candidates for an image preload link.

Watch for: Use compatible candidate descriptors and pair its semantics with the later img request.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-imagesrcset

### A068 inert definition

`inert`. Make a subtree inert for applicable user interaction and focus behavior. It is boolean.

Watch for: It does not authorize access or remove source data; consider modal and flat-tree behavior.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#the-inert-attribute

### A069 inputmode definition

`inputmode`. Hint the entry modality using text, tel, email, url, numeric, decimal, search or none.

Watch for: A numeric keyboard hint accepts no validation responsibility and does not turn text into a number.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: "none"; "text"; "tel"; "email"; "url"; "numeric"; "decimal"; "search".

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#attr-inputmode

### A070 integrity definition

`integrity`. Supply Subresource Integrity hashes for an eligible script or stylesheet resource.

Watch for: The hash must match exact served bytes; cross-origin checks also need the appropriate CORS response.

Context: link; script. Value grammar: Text.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-integrity

### A071 is definition

`is`. Request a defined customized built-in element at creation, using its registered custom-element name.

Watch for: Changing is later does not upgrade an ordinary element into the requested built-in; support needs checking.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#attr-is

### A072 ismap definition

`ismap`. Declare an image as part of a server-side image map in its permitted anchor context.

Watch for: It is not the client-side usemap mechanism and still needs an understandable navigation alternative.

Context: img. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#attr-img-ismap

### A073 itemid definition

`itemid`. Provide a global identifier for a microdata item where the vocabulary and item context allow it.

Watch for: An item ID is metadata, not the DOM id attribute or a security credential.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/microdata.html#attr-itemid

### A074 itemprop definition

`itemprop`. Attach one or more microdata property names to an element. The value is derived from the element-specific microdata rules.

Watch for: Do not assume every property takes its value from textContent.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens consisting of valid absolute URLs, defined property names, or text*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/microdata.html#names:-the-itemprop-attribute

### A075 itemref definition

`itemref`. Reference additional elements by ID for a microdata item's properties.

Watch for: Resolve IDs in the intended scope and avoid cycles or accidental unrelated properties.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens consisting of IDs*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/microdata.html#attr-itemref

### A076 itemscope definition

`itemscope`. Start a microdata item. This boolean changes the metadata grouping of descendant properties.

Watch for: It does not instantiate a JavaScript object or validate a vocabulary.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/microdata.html#attr-itemscope

### A077 itemtype definition

`itemtype`. Declare microdata type URLs on an item.

Watch for: The vocabulary is separate from HTML; a declared type does not guarantee a rich search result.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens consisting of valid absolute URLs*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/microdata.html#attr-itemtype

### A078 kind definition

`kind`. Choose the text track category: subtitles, captions, descriptions, chapters or metadata.

Watch for: A kind keyword does not generate the necessary timed text.

Context: track. Value grammar: "subtitles"; "captions"; "descriptions"; "chapters"; "metadata".

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#attr-track-kind

### A079 label definition

`label`. Provide an optgroup's group label, an option's display label or a track's user-visible label.

Watch for: It is not the label element's for association.

Context: optgroup; option; track. Value grammar: Text.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-optgroup-label

### A080 lang definition

`lang`. Declare the human language using a BCP 47 language tag, with inheritance where applicable.

Watch for: It can help pronunciation and processing; it does not translate content.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Valid BCP 47 language tag or the empty string.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#attr-lang

### A081 list definition

`list`. Reference a datalist by ID for suggestions on applicable input states.

Watch for: It is not a closed-value constraint and is ignored on incompatible types.

Context: input. Value grammar: ID*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-list

### A082 loading definition

`loading`. Hint eager or lazy deferral for eligible img, iframe and, in the observed current standard, audio or video elements.

Watch for: This newer media application requires target testing; avoid delaying a resource essential to the initial task.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#attr-iframe-loading

### A083 loop definition

`loop`. Repeat media playback after completion where applicable. It is boolean.

Watch for: A loop can affect ended-event expectations and user control needs.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#attr-media-loop

### A084 low definition

`low`. On meter, set the end of the low-value subrange.

Watch for: Interpret it with the full min, max, high and optimum configuration.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-meter-low

`max`. On applicable inputs, set an upper value bound in that type's grammar. On meter and progress, define a numeric upper range bound.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-max

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-meter-max

### A086 maxlength definition

`maxlength`. Limit text length for applicable input types and textarea under the platform's UTF-16 code-unit rules.

Watch for: It does not count user-perceived grapheme clusters and is not a server validation boundary.

### A087 media definition

`media`. Condition an eligible link, style, meta theme-color or source by a media query list in the applicable context.

Watch for: Do not assume the attribute has an effect for every meta name or source use.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-media

### A088 method definition

`method`. Choose form get, post or dialog behavior. Missing or invalid form method values use get under the normal rules.

Watch for: POST is not encryption; use HTTPS and validate on the server.

Context: form. Value grammar: "get"; "post"; "dialog".

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-method

### A089 min definition

`min`. On applicable inputs, set the lower bound in that type's grammar. On meter, define its lower numeric range bound.

Watch for: The type controls syntax, defaults and step-base behavior.

Context: meter. Value grammar: Valid floating-point number*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-meter-min

### A090 minlength definition

`minlength`. Set a minimum applicable text length in UTF-16 code units.

Watch for: An optional empty field is not made required solely by minlength.

Context: input; textarea. Value grammar: Valid non-negative integer.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-minlength

### A091 multiple definition

`multiple`. Allow multiple values on select and applicable email or file input states.

`muted`. Set the default muted state of audio or video. The live muted property and defaultMuted need separate reasoning.

`name`. Identify a control's submission key or API name, a form, a browsing target, a map, a slot, metadata, or a details exclusivity group depending on the element.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-meta-name

### A094 nomodule definition

`nomodule`. Skip a classic fallback script in environments supporting modules. It is boolean.

Watch for: This is not a declaration that the script itself is a module.

### A095 nonce definition

`nonce`. Carry a server-generated cryptographic nonce authorized by an actual Content Security Policy.

### A096 novalidate definition

`novalidate`. Bypass a form's interactive constraint-validation step during submission. It is boolean.

### A097 open definition

`open`. Set the expanded state of details or the showing state of dialog. It is boolean.

### A098 optimum definition

`optimum`. On meter, identify the best value so low and high subranges can be interpreted.

`pattern`. Require an applicable nonempty input value to match the whole regular expression using current Unicode-aware v-flag rules.

### A100 ping definition

`ping`. List space-separated URLs that can receive hyperlink-auditing notifications when a link is followed.

### A101 placeholder definition

`placeholder`. Supply a short entry hint inside compatible controls.

### A102 playsinline definition

`playsinline`. Encourage video playback within its element's area. It is boolean.

### A103 popover definition

`popover`. Create a popover state using auto, manual or hint, with empty meaning auto under current rules.

### A104 popovertarget definition

`popovertarget`. Reference the ID of a popover target from an eligible button or input button control.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#attr-popovertarget

### A105 popovertargetaction definition

`popovertargetaction`. Choose toggle, show or hide for the target popover.

Watch for: It does not create dialog modality or a complete menu keyboard model.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#attr-popovertargetaction

### A106 poster definition

`poster`. Set the video preview image URL.

Watch for: A poster does not replace the video's captions, transcript or source resources.

### A107 preload definition

`preload`. Hint none, metadata or auto media buffering, with the defined empty-value behavior.

### A108 readonly definition

`readonly`. Prevent user edits on applicable textual controls while preserving relevant submission behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#attr-face-readonly

### A109 referrerpolicy definition

`referrerpolicy`. Select which referrer information accompanies eligible requests.

### A110 rel definition

`rel`. Describe link relationships using permitted space-separated tokens; eligible form relationships have their own defined subset.

### A111 required definition

`required`. Require a value or selection in an applicable control. Radios have group rules and selects have placeholder-option rules.

### A112 reversed definition

`reversed`. Number an ordered list in descending order. It is boolean.

`rows`. Suggest textarea's visible line count using a positive integer.

`sandbox`. Apply iframe restrictions; its tokens selectively relax capabilities such as scripts, forms, downloads, popups or navigation.

Watch for: An empty value applies the restriction set. Granting scripts and same-origin to hostile same-origin content can undermine the boundary.

Context: iframe. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens, ASCII case-insensitive, consisting of "allow-downloads"; "allow-forms"; "allow-modals"; "allow-orientation-lock"; "allow-pointer-lock"; "allow-popups"; "allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox"; "allow-presentation"; "allow-same-origin"; "allow-scripts"; "allow-top-navigation"; "allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation"; "allow-top-navigation-to-custom-protocols".

### A117 scope definition

`scope`. On th, identify row, col, rowgroup or colgroup relationships.

Context: th. Value grammar: "row"; "col"; "rowgroup"; "colgroup".

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#attr-th-scope

### A118 selected definition

`selected`. Declare an option's default selectedness. It is boolean.

Watch for: The selected property tracks current state; defaultSelected reflects markup.

Context: option. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-option-selected

### A119 shadowrootclonable definition

`shadowrootclonable`. Configure a declarative shadow root to be clonable under the applicable root-creation rules.

Watch for: It does not clone a component by itself; test newer root options in the target engine.

Context: template. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#attr-template-shadowrootclonable

### A120 shadowrootcustomelementregistry definition

`shadowrootcustomelementregistry`. Configure a declarative shadow root to use a custom element registry under the current standard's registry rules.

### A121 shadowrootdelegatesfocus definition

`shadowrootdelegatesfocus`. Request delegated focus for a declarative shadow root. It is boolean.

### A122 shadowrootmode definition

`shadowrootmode`. Create a declarative shadow root using open or closed at the valid parse location.

### A123 shadowrootserializable definition

`shadowrootserializable`. Allow a declarative shadow root to participate in the relevant serialization APIs.

Watch for: Serialization and privacy are different concerns; closed roots are not a security boundary.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#attr-template-shadowrootserializable

### A124 shadowrootslotassignment definition

`shadowrootslotassignment`. Select named or manual slot assignment for the declarative shadow root.

Watch for: Manual assignment requires the applicable DOM API and current engine support.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#attr-template-shadowrootslotassignment

### A125 shape definition

`shape`. Select rect, circle, poly or default geometry for an image-map area.

Watch for: Use the corresponding coords grammar and test actual hit targets.

Context: area. Value grammar: "circle"; "default"; "poly"; "rect".

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/image-maps.html#attr-area-shape

### A126 size definition

`size`. Set an applicable text-input width or select's displayed-size behavior using its own positive integer rules.

Watch for: It is not maxlength, CSS width or a multi-value permission.

Context: input; select. Value grammar: Valid non-negative integer greater than zero.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-size

### A127 sizes definition

`sizes`. For img and picture source, describe image source sizes; for link rel=icon, list available icon dimensions or any.

Watch for: Image source-size syntax and icon-size syntax are unrelated despite the shared name.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-sizes

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#attr-img-sizes

### A128 slot definition

`slot`. Assign a light-DOM node to a named slot in a shadow host; an empty name targets the default slot.

Watch for: This attribute and the slot element's name connect different sides of projection.

### A129 span definition

`span`. Set how many columns a col or colgroup describes in its applicable mode.

Watch for: It is unrelated to the span element and does not create data cells.

### A130 spellcheck definition

`spellcheck`. Recommend spelling and grammar checking using true or false, with an empty value treated under its enumerated rules.

Watch for: It does not enforce language correctness or reliably prevent remote processing by all input tools.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#attr-spellcheck

### A131 src definition

`src`. Choose a resource address on the eligible media, image, embed, iframe, script, track or input-image element.

Watch for: Its loading and security behavior depends on the consumer and resource type.

### A132 srcdoc definition

`srcdoc`. Provide an iframe's inline HTML document. It takes precedence over src in the relevant processing mode.

Watch for: Treat untrusted content as HTML injection and use an appropriate sandbox and serving policy.

Context: iframe. Value grammar: The source of an iframe srcdoc document*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#attr-iframe-srcdoc

### A133 srclang definition

`srclang`. Identify a track's language with a valid language tag; subtitles require it.

Watch for: It names the track language, not the parent document or spoken audio automatically.

Context: track. Value grammar: Valid BCP 47 language tag.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#attr-track-srclang

### A134 srcset definition

`srcset`. Offer image candidates with compatible width or density descriptors.

Watch for: A width list needs meaningful source sizes; the browser chooses candidates rather than following a fixed screenshot expectation.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#attr-img-srcset

### A135 start definition

`start`. Set an ordered list's initial ordinal using an integer, including a negative value when appropriate.

Watch for: It changes numbering rather than reordering items.

Context: ol. Value grammar: Valid integer.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#attr-ol-start

### A136 step definition

`step`. Set an applicable input's increment as a positive number or any. Defaults and the step base depend on input type.

Watch for: Min, value and type can influence the base, so an apparently round value can still be a step mismatch.

Context: input. Value grammar: Valid floating-point number greater than zero, or "any".

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-step

### A137 style definition

`style`. Supply CSS declarations on the element. The style DOM property exposes a declaration object.

Watch for: It changes presentation; it does not change the content model or sanitize a CSS string.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: CSS declarations*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#attr-style

### A138 tabindex definition

`tabindex`. Control focusability and sequential focus ordering through an integer. Zero follows normal ordering; negative values remove ordinary sequential entry while permitting relevant focus behavior.

Watch for: Avoid positive ordering as a routine layout repair, and do not make hidden controls focusable.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Valid integer.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#attr-tabindex

### A139 target definition

`target`. Choose where a or area navigates, where a form submits, or the default on base.

Watch for: _self, _blank, _parent and _top have distinct meanings; a new context is a deliberate user-experience choice.

Context: a; area. Value grammar: Valid navigable target name or keyword.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#attr-hyperlink-target

Context: base. Value grammar: Valid navigable target name or keyword.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-base-target

Context: form. Value grammar: Valid navigable target name or keyword.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-target

### A140 title definition

`title`. Provide advisory text, or a context-specific expansion or stylesheet title. Some elements specialize its meaning.

Watch for: It is not a dependable substitute for a label, visible instructions or image alternatives.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Text.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#attr-title

Context: abbr; dfn. Value grammar: Text.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#attr-abbr-title

Context: input. Value grammar: Text.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-title

Context: link. Value grammar: Text.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-title

Context: link; style. Value grammar: Text.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-title

### A141 translate definition

`translate`. Specify whether text and applicable attribute values should be translated, using yes or no; empty means yes.

Watch for: It is guidance for localization tooling, not an access or privacy control.

Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: "yes"; "no"; the empty string.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#attr-translate

### A142 type definition

`type`. Select the specialized mode of input, button, script, ol or an embedded resource, or supply a MIME hint for a link.

Watch for: Each element defines its own keyword space; type="button" is not a MIME type.

Context: a; link. Value grammar: Valid MIME type string.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#attr-hyperlink-type

Context: button. Value grammar: "submit"; "reset"; "button".

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-button-type

Context: embed; object; source. Value grammar: Valid MIME type string.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#attr-embed-type

Context: input. Value grammar: input type keyword.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-type

Context: ol. Value grammar: "1"; "a"; "A"; "i"; "I".

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#attr-ol-type

### A143 usemap definition

`usemap`. Reference a named client-side image map with a hash-name reference.

Watch for: It points to map.name rather than assuming any nearby map is used.

Context: img. Value grammar: Valid hash-name reference*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/image-maps.html#attr-hyperlink-usemap

### A144 value definition

`value`. Supply a control's default or submitted string, a list item's ordinal, data's machine value, or meter/progress's number depending on the element.

Watch for: A DOM property named value may represent current state rather than a live reflection of markup.

Context: button; option. Value grammar: Text.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-button-value

Context: data. Value grammar: Text*.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/text-level-semantics.html#attr-data-value

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-value

### A145 width definition

`width`. Set an eligible horizontal dimension; canvas uses backing coordinates while image/video dimensions can reserve layout space.

Watch for: CSS scaling can change display size without changing resource resolution or canvas drawing coordinates.

### A146 wrap definition

`wrap`. Choose soft or hard textarea submission wrapping.

Watch for: Hard wrapping depends on the relevant width configuration and is not just a visual CSS effect.

Context: textarea. Value grammar: "soft"; "hard".

### A147 writingsuggestions definition

`writingsuggestions`. Recommend whether writing suggestions are offered using true or false and the defined empty-value behavior.

Watch for: It is separate from spellcheck, autocorrect and application-generated completions.

## 5 Complete current element catalogue

All 113 current HTML element names have an entry below. The attributes line gives exact dictionary IDs for element-specific settings and important specialized shared attributes. Every entry also uses the shared families in Part 3. No additional element-specific attributes means exactly that; global attributes and applicable event-handler families remain available.

The content-model summary is a navigation aid, not the full normative model. An asterisk in a summary indicates context-dependent restrictions in the linked definition. Flow describes general document content; phrasing describes text-level content; transparent means to apply the surrounding model with the element's additional restrictions; script-supporting content refers to the permitted script/template mechanisms. Read the linked detailed definition before building a strict validator.

### Document metadata

#### Element html

`<html>`. The document root contains the head and body. Set the page language here so descendants inherit it; use direction separately when needed.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLHtmlElement`. Context summary: parents none*; children head*; body*.

```html
<html lang="en"> ... </html>
```

Common mistake: A missing language declaration is not repaired by a translated page title.

Practice: explain why `html` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-html-element

#### Element head

`<head>`. Collect document metadata rather than visible page structure. A normal standalone document needs a useful title and an early encoding declaration.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLHeadElement`. Context summary: parents html; children metadata content*.

```html
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Field notebook</title></head>
```

Common mistake: Putting visible headings here causes parsing surprises rather than creating a second header.

Practice: explain why `head` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-head-element

#### Element title

`<title>`. Name the document for tabs, history and other consumers. Write text that distinguishes this page from neighboring pages.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLTitleElement`. Context summary: parents head; children text*.

```html
<title>Reserve a desk at Cedar Library</title>
```

Common mistake: This is not the page's visible h1 and does not promise a search-engine title.

Practice: explain why `title` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-title-element

#### Element base

`<base>`. Set the base URL for resolving relative URLs and optionally a default navigation target. Its effect reaches links, images and even fragment references.

Attributes: `href` (A062); `target` (A139). Read the named definitions in Part 4; type and context restrictions still apply.

DOM interface: `HTMLBaseElement`. Context summary: parents head; children empty.

```html
<base href="https://example.org/guides/">
```

Common mistake: Do not introduce a base element to patch one broken link without checking every relative reference.

Practice: explain why `base` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-base-element

#### Element link

`<link>`. Describe a relationship to an external resource, such as a stylesheet, icon or preload. The rel value determines which other attributes make sense.

Attributes: `href` (A062); `crossorigin` (A034); `rel` (A110); `media` (A087); `integrity` (A070); `hreflang` (A063); `type` (A142); `referrerpolicy` (A109); `sizes` (A127); `imagesrcset` (A067); `imagesizes` (A066); `as` (A011); `blocking` (A018); `color` (A024); `disabled` (A043); `fetchpriority` (A048); `title` (A140). Read the named definitions in Part 4; type and context restrictions still apply.

DOM interface: `HTMLLinkElement`. Context summary: parents head; noscript*; phrasing*; children empty.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
```

Common mistake: A link preload downloads a resource; it does not apply a stylesheet or execute a script by itself.

Practice: explain why `link` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-link-element

#### Element meta

`<meta>`. Express metadata through a named value, selected pragma, or encoding declaration. Choose one applicable metadata mode rather than combining unrelated modes.

Attributes: `name` (A093); `http-equiv` (A064); `content` (A030); `charset` (A019); `media` (A087). Read the named definitions in Part 4; type and context restrictions still apply.

DOM interface: `HTMLMetaElement`. Context summary: parents head; noscript*; phrasing*; children empty.

```html
<meta name="description" content="A guide to accessible field notebooks">
```

Common mistake: A viewport declaration does not make an unresponsive layout responsive or enforce access control.

Practice: explain why `meta` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-meta-element

#### Element style

`<style>`. Embed a stylesheet. Its text is CSS, so selector syntax and cascade behavior belong to the CSS layer.

Attributes: `media` (A087); `blocking` (A018); `title` (A140). Read the named definitions in Part 4; type and context restrictions still apply.

DOM interface: `HTMLStyleElement`. Context summary: parents head; noscript*; flow*; children text*.

```html
<style>strong { color: #5b2400; }</style>
```

Common mistake: Use CSS for presentation without changing the semantic purpose of the chosen element.

Practice: explain why `style` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-style-element

#### Element body

`<body>`. Contain document content. Some handler attributes written on body are actually handlers for the Window object and are catalogued separately.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

Window handler aliases: `onafterprint`, `onbeforeprint`, `onbeforeunload`, `onhashchange`, `onlanguagechange`, `onmessage`, `onmessageerror`, `onoffline`, `ononline`, `onpagehide`, `onpagereveal`, `onpageshow`, `onpageswap`, `onpopstate`, `onrejectionhandled`, `onstorage`, `onunhandledrejection`, `onunload`. Each is explained in Part 7.

DOM interface: `HTMLBodyElement`. Context summary: parents html; children flow.

```html
<body><h1>Field notes</h1><p>Record today's route.</p></body>
```

Common mistake: Use a header within the body for introductory content; body itself is not a banner.

Practice: explain why `body` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-body-element

### Sections and landmarks

#### Element article

`<article>`. Identify a self-contained composition, such as an article, forum post or independently meaningful entry. Give its content a useful heading when appropriate.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLElement`. Context summary: parents flow; children flow.

```html
<article><h2>Watching the estuary</h2><p>Visit at low tide.</p></article>
```

Common mistake: Do not use article for every layout card when the content has no independent meaning.

Practice: explain why `article` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-article-element

#### Element section

`<section>`. Group a thematic portion of a document. A heading usually explains the section's topic; structure follows meaning rather than visual borders.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLElement`. Context summary: parents flow; children flow.

```html
<section><h2>Equipment</h2><p>Bring binoculars.</p></section>
```

Common mistake: Nesting sections does not automatically correct arbitrary h1 through h6 ranks for users.

Practice: explain why `section` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-section-element

#### Element nav

`<nav>`. Identify a major navigation region. Label repeated navigation regions so users can distinguish their purpose.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLElement`. Context summary: parents flow; children flow.

```html
<nav aria-label="Guide"><a href="routes.html">Routes</a></nav>
```

Common mistake: Not every collection of links needs its own nav; use the region when navigation is its purpose.

Practice: explain why `nav` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-nav-element

#### Element aside

`<aside>`. Mark content tangentially related to surrounding material, such as related reading. Its placement on the screen is a separate CSS choice.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLElement`. Context summary: parents flow; children flow.

```html
<aside><h2>Related reading</h2><a href="birds.html">Bird guide</a></aside>
```

Common mistake: A sidebar layout alone does not make its content an aside.

Practice: explain why `aside` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-aside-element

#### Element h1

`<h1>`. Express a top-level heading. Select rank from the document's topic hierarchy and give the page a clear primary topic.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLHeadingElement`. Context summary: parents legend; summary; flow; children phrasing.

```html
<h1>Estuary visitor guide</h1>
```

Common mistake: Do not select heading rank for its default font size.

Practice: explain why `h1` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements

#### Element h2

`<h2>`. Express a second-level heading below the relevant higher-level topic. It commonly introduces major sections within a page.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLHeadingElement`. Context summary: parents legend; summary; flow; children phrasing.

```html
<h2>Planning your visit</h2>
```

Common mistake: A bold paragraph does not become a heading in the document structure.

Practice: explain why `h2` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements

#### Element h3

`<h3>`. Express a third-level heading for a subsection. Keep the relationship to its parent topic intelligible when headings are read alone.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLHeadingElement`. Context summary: parents legend; summary; flow; children phrasing.

```html
<h3>Choosing a route</h3>
```

Common mistake: Do not jump to h3 just because a design calls for smaller text.

Practice: explain why `h3` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements

#### Element h4

`<h4>`. Express a fourth-level heading when the material genuinely needs that depth. Consider whether restructuring would make the content easier to navigate.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLHeadingElement`. Context summary: parents legend; summary; flow; children phrasing.

```html
<h4>Routes with level surfaces</h4>
```

Common mistake: Deep nesting can be valid yet hard to understand; inspect the resulting outline.

Practice: explain why `h4` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements

#### Element h5

`<h5>`. Express a fifth-level heading in a deeply structured document. It still conveys heading semantics and is not a caption shortcut.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLHeadingElement`. Context summary: parents legend; summary; flow; children phrasing.

```html
<h5>Boardwalk surface details</h5>
```

Common mistake: A visual caption should not receive h5 merely to reduce its size.

Practice: explain why `h5` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#the-h1,-h2,-h3,-h4,-h5,-and-h6-elements

#### Element h6

`<h6>`. Express a sixth-level heading. This is the lowest numbered native heading element, not a generic small-text element.

Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.

DOM interface: `HTMLHeadingElement`. Context summary: parents legend; summary; flow; children phrasing.

```html
<h6>Maintenance inspection notes</h6>
```

<p><del datetime="2026-10-16">Use the west bridge.</del></p>

#### Element img

#### Element embed

`<embed>`. Embed an external resource through the browser's supported handling. Prefer a more specific native element when it provides the required semantics and alternatives.

#### Element video

#### Element track

`<track>`. Supply timed text to audio or video. Choose kind, language and label to describe actual track content.

`<map>`. Define an image map named for an img usemap reference. Area links need meaningful alternatives, and the image still needs its own context.

`<table>`. Represent relationships in tabular data. Design header associations and a useful caption before styling rows and columns.

`<caption>`. Give a table a title or explanation as its table child. It provides context that a reader can use while navigating the table.

`<colgroup>`. Group columns, optionally with col children, or use span to specify a group without children. It can support shared column styling.

`<col>`. Describe one or more columns in a colgroup. Only a limited set of CSS column effects applies; it is not a cell container.

## 6 Input types and attribute applicability

The type attribute selects one of the following 22 states. Unknown or missing type normally falls back to text. The input attribute list is a union of capabilities across states, not permission to use every attribute on every state. An input remains a void element regardless of type.

### Input type hidden

`type="hidden"`. Stores a non-visible submitted value; it is not an interactive text field.

name and value are central; hidden values are visible to clients and must be validated by the server.

### Input type text

`type="text"`. Accepts single-line plain text with text-specific constraints.

Use minlength, maxlength, pattern and placeholder where useful; label remains persistent.

### Input type search

`type="search"`. Accepts a single-line search query.

Its search purpose can affect native presentation; results still require a submission or application workflow.

### Input type tel

`type="tel"`. Accepts a telephone string without a universal built-in telephone grammar.

Use an appropriate autocomplete token and visible format guidance rather than assuming all countries share a pattern.

### Input type url

`type="url"`. Accepts a URL with URL-state validation.

Syntax acceptance is not a safe allowlist for destinations and does not fetch the URL.

### Input type email

`type="email"`. Accepts an email string, or a comma-separated list with multiple.

The platform syntax check does not establish mailbox existence or ownership.

### Input type password

`type="password"`. Accepts a masked text string.

Use current-password or new-password autocomplete appropriately; masking is not encryption.

### Input type date

`type="date"`. Accepts a calendar date, serialized as year-month-day under the date grammar.

Display can be localized; do not parse the visible date format as if it were the value string.

### Input type month

`type="month"`. Accepts a year and month.

Min, max and step use month-state rules rather than day units.

### Input type week

`type="week"`. Accepts a week-year and week number in the defined week format.

Week years do not always match the calendar year of every included day.

### Input type time

`type="time"`. Accepts a time without an associated date or time zone.

Step is measured using time-state units; an optional seconds component changes precision.

### Input type datetime-local

`type="datetime-local"`. Accepts a local date and time without a time-zone offset.

An appointment system must separately decide the relevant zone and daylight-saving rules.

### Input type number

`type="number"`. Accepts a numeric quantity with number-state validation and stepping.

Use min, max and step for quantities; use text for identifiers whose leading zeros matter.

### Input type range

`type="range"`. Selects a numeric value within an effective range.

Defaults and clamping differ from number; add a label and an output if users need the exact current value.

### Input type color

`type="color"`. Selects a color; the current standard includes colorspace and alpha settings.

Serialization can vary with the configured space; newer color features need target-browser checks.

### Input type checkbox

`type="checkbox"`. Represents an independent checked state.

Only checked controls contribute normal entries; absent value commonly yields on. required applies to that checkbox.

### Input type radio

`type="radio"`. Selects one checked choice within its group.

Grouping depends on name, form ownership and tree rules; required operates through group constraints.

### Input type file

`type="file"`. Lets the user select files.

accept is a chooser hint; multiple permits several files. The value property cannot assign an arbitrary local file path.

### Input type submit

`type="submit"`. Activates form submission and can contribute its own name/value as the submitter.

formaction, formenctype, formmethod, formnovalidate and formtarget apply in this context.

### Input type image

`type="image"`. Submits through an image control and contributes activation coordinates under image-submit rules.

Provide alt and src; width and height describe the image. Its payload differs from an ordinary submit button.

### Input type reset

`type="reset"`. Resets eligible associated controls to their defaults.

Reset is not a save or clear-everything operation and can discard user edits unexpectedly.

### Input type button

`type="button"`. Creates a push button without an inherent submission action.

Use value for its visible label; application code or a permitted popover relationship supplies the intended action.

### State by state content attribute map

The following map transposes the specification summary into readable groups. It lists the input-specific content attributes evaluated by that summary. Common disabled, form, name and type settings and the shared attribute families remain separate. Value has state-specific modes. Conditional annotations retain the summary meaning; consult the defining type section for edge cases.

- Hidden: `autocomplete`, `dirname`.

- Text, Search: `autocomplete`, `dirname`, `list`, `maxlength`, `minlength`, `pattern`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `required`, `size`.

- Telephone, URL: `autocomplete`, `dirname`, `list`, `maxlength`, `minlength`, `pattern`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `required`, `size`.

- Email: `autocomplete`, `dirname`, `list`, `maxlength`, `minlength`, `multiple`, `pattern`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `required`, `size`.

- Password: `autocomplete`, `dirname`, `maxlength`, `minlength`, `pattern`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `required`, `size`.

- Date, Month, Week, Time: `autocomplete`, `list`, `max`, `min`, `readonly`, `required`, `step`.

- Local Date and Time: `autocomplete`, `list`, `max`, `min`, `readonly`, `required`, `step`.

- Number: `autocomplete`, `list`, `max`, `min`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `required`, `step`.

- Range: `autocomplete`, `list`, `max`, `min`, `step`.

- Color: `alpha`, `autocomplete`, `colorspace`, `list`.

- Checkbox, Radio Button: `checked`, `required`.

- File Upload: `accept`, `multiple`, `required`.

- Submit Button: `dirname`, `formaction`, `formenctype`, `formmethod`, `formnovalidate`, `formtarget`, `popovertarget`, `popovertargetaction`.

- Image Button: `alt`, `formaction`, `formenctype`, `formmethod`, `formnovalidate`, `formtarget`, `height`, `popovertarget`, `popovertargetaction`, `src`, `width`.

- Reset Button, Button: `popovertarget`, `popovertargetaction`.


Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#input-type-attr-summary

### Applicability rules to learn together

- Pattern and text-length constraints apply to the compatible text-like states, not number, date, file or checkbox. A number field uses min, max and step rather than pattern.
- Readonly applies to text-like and supported date/time/number states, not to checkbox, radio, range, color, file or button states. Disabled is a different control state.
- Multiple applies to email and file input; select has its own multiple attribute. Required applies to supported value and selection states, not hidden, range, color or action buttons.
- Checked applies to checkbox and radio defaults. Accept applies to file. Alpha and colorspace apply to color. Alt, src, width and height apply to image submitters.
- Submitter overrides apply to submit and image input states. Popover targeting applies to an eligible button state rather than every input.
- List supplies suggestions only for compatible states. Text-selection APIs such as selectionStart and setSelectionRange also have a narrower applicability set than all inputs.
- Hidden input has special submission cases such as _charset_; radio names define groups, while a checkbox name is a submission key and does not create radio exclusivity.

## 7 Complete indexed HTML event handler attributes

The observed HTML index lists 89 handler attributes. Each on-prefixed content attribute holds a JavaScript handler body, not the name of a callback function by magic. Prefer addEventListener in scripts so behavior is separate from markup and compatible with a deliberate CSP. An IDL property such as onclick normally holds one handler; listeners added with addEventListener use separate listener registration.

Global availability does not mean an event fires on every element. Some events do not bubble, some are not cancelable, and body aliases several Window handlers. PreventDefault affects a cancelable default action, while stopPropagation affects propagation; neither substitutes for the other. Programmatic dispatch does not confer trusted user activation or guarantee privileged browser behavior.

### onafterprint

`onafterprint` handles `afterprint`. Window has finished the applicable print or preview process; restore temporary presentation if needed.

Declared context: body. Prefer `afterprint` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onauxclick

`onauxclick` handles `auxclick`. A non-primary pointing-device button was activated; it is distinct from the ordinary primary click.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `auxclick` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onbeforeinput

`onbeforeinput` handles `beforeinput`. An editing operation is about to change input content; inspect inputType and cancellation rules rather than assuming every operation is cancelable.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `beforeinput` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onbeforematch

`onbeforematch` handles `beforematch`. Content hidden until found is about to be revealed through the relevant find or fragment process.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `beforematch` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onbeforeprint

`onbeforeprint` handles `beforeprint`. Window is entering an applicable print or preview process; prefer print CSS for ordinary styling.

Declared context: body. Prefer `beforeprint` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onbeforeunload

`onbeforeunload` handles `beforeunload`. The page is being considered for departure; conditional unsaved-change prompts are constrained and unreliable as a persistence mechanism.

Declared context: body. Prefer `beforeunload` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onbeforetoggle

`onbeforetoggle` handles `beforetoggle`. A supported showing or disclosure transition is pending; inspect oldState, newState and whether this transition can be canceled.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `beforetoggle` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onblur

`onblur` handles `blur`. The relevant focus target lost focus; ordinary blur does not bubble like focusout.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `blur` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oncancel

`oncancel` handles `cancel`. A dialog or another supported control receives its defined cancellation event; inspect the target and cancelability.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `cancel` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oncanplay

`oncanplay` handles `canplay`. Media has enough data to begin playback under the relevant readiness rules; future uninterrupted playback is not guaranteed.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `canplay` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oncanplaythrough

`oncanplaythrough` handles `canplaythrough`. The media element estimates that playback can continue through the end; this is an estimate rather than a network guarantee.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `canplaythrough` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onchange

`onchange` handles `change`. A control commits a changed value under its type-specific interaction rules; it need not fire on every keystroke.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `change` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onclick

`onclick` handles `click`. Activation occurred through a supported click path, including native keyboard activation where applicable.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `click` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onclose

`onclose` handles `close`. A supported dialog close has completed; inspect returnValue on the dialog rather than inventing a submission.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `close` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oncommand

`oncommand` handles `command`. A command invoker dispatched a command to its target; custom commands need application handling.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `command` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oncontextlost

`oncontextlost` handles `contextlost`. The canvas rendering context was lost; preserve application data needed to redraw.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `contextlost` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oncontextmenu

`oncontextmenu` handles `contextmenu`. A context-menu request occurred; preventing the native menu has usability consequences.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `contextmenu` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oncontextrestored

`oncontextrestored` handles `contextrestored`. A lost canvas context was restored; recreate rendering state as required.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `contextrestored` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oncopy

`oncopy` handles `copy`. A copy operation targets the selection or editable context; clipboard permissions and default behavior still matter.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `copy` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oncuechange

`oncuechange` handles `cuechange`. Active timed-text cues changed on a text track; use the track interface to inspect them.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `cuechange` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oncut

`oncut` handles `cut`. A cut operation is requested; altering clipboard data and editing are separate parts of its default behavior.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `cut` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### ondblclick

`ondblclick` handles `dblclick`. A supported double-click interaction occurred; keep essential actions available without requiring this gesture.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `dblclick` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### ondrag

`ondrag` handles `drag`. The drag source is being dragged during a drag-and-drop operation.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `drag` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### ondragend

`ondragend` handles `dragend`. The drag operation ended; clean up transient source state.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `dragend` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### ondragenter

`ondragenter` handles `dragenter`. A drag entered a potential drop target; nested targets can produce several transitions.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `dragenter` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### ondragleave

`ondragleave` handles `dragleave`. A drag left the relevant target; avoid confusing child-boundary transitions with leaving the whole region.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `dragleave` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### ondragover

`ondragover` handles `dragover`. A drag is over a potential target; accepting a drop commonly requires canceling this event's default behavior.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `dragover` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### ondragstart

`ondragstart` handles `dragstart`. A drag began at the source; configure DataTransfer with the intended payload and allowed effect.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `dragstart` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### ondrop

`ondrop` handles `drop`. A drop occurred on an accepting target; validate the dropped data and retain a keyboard-accessible alternative.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `drop` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### ondurationchange

`ondurationchange` handles `durationchange`. The media duration value changed, including transitions from unknown metadata.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `durationchange` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onemptied

`onemptied` handles `emptied`. The media element became empty through its resource-state processing.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `emptied` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onended

`onended` handles `ended`. Playback reached its defined end; loop configuration can change when this event is expected.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `ended` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onerror

`onerror` handles `error`. A resource or execution error occurred under the target-specific event rules; this is not a universal detailed diagnostic object.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `error` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onfocus

`onfocus` handles `focus`. The target received focus; ordinary focus does not bubble like focusin.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `focus` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onformdata

`onformdata` handles `formdata`. A form entry list was constructed and is exposed through FormDataEvent for permitted inspection or modification.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `formdata` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onhashchange

`onhashchange` handles `hashchange`. Window's URL fragment changed through a path that fires this event; pushState does not simply reproduce it.

Declared context: body. Prefer `hashchange` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oninput

`oninput` handles `input`. A control or editable region changed through an applicable user-editing path; assigning value in script does not automatically fire it.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `input` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### oninvalid

`oninvalid` handles `invalid`. A control failed an applicable validity check; it does not bubble as an ordinary submit handler would.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `invalid` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onkeydown

`onkeydown` handles `keydown`. A key was pressed; inspect key, modifiers, repeat and composition context before overriding native behavior.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `keydown` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onkeypress

`onkeypress` handles `keypress`. A legacy keyboard event retained for compatibility; use current key or editing events for new code.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `keypress` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onkeyup

`onkeyup` handles `keyup`. A key was released; it is not a reliable standalone signal that text changed.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `keyup` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onlanguagechange

`onlanguagechange` handles `languagechange`. Window's preferred language settings changed under the applicable environment behavior.

Declared context: body. Prefer `languagechange` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onload

`onload` handles `load`. The target completed its defined loading step; it is not a generic proof that all descendants or application work succeeded.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `load` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onloadeddata

`onloadeddata` handles `loadeddata`. Media data for the current playback position became available under its readiness transition.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `loadeddata` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onloadedmetadata

`onloadedmetadata` handles `loadedmetadata`. Media metadata such as dimensions and duration became available.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `loadedmetadata` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onloadstart

`onloadstart` handles `loadstart`. The media element began a resource selection or loading process.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `loadstart` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onmessage

`onmessage` handles `message`. Window received a postMessage message; verify source, origin and payload before using it.

Declared context: body. Prefer `message` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onmessageerror

`onmessageerror` handles `messageerror`. A received message could not be deserialized under the messaging rules.

Declared context: body. Prefer `messageerror` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onmousedown

`onmousedown` handles `mousedown`. A mouse button was pressed; it is distinct from click activation and does not cover every input modality.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `mousedown` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onmouseenter

`onmouseenter` handles `mouseenter`. The mouse entered the target boundary; its propagation differs from mouseover.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `mouseenter` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onmouseleave

`onmouseleave` handles `mouseleave`. The mouse left the target boundary; its propagation differs from mouseout.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `mouseleave` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onmousemove

`onmousemove` handles `mousemove`. The mouse moved over the relevant target; avoid unnecessary expensive work on every event.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `mousemove` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onmouseout

`onmouseout` handles `mouseout`. The mouse left the target for another target, including relevant descendant-boundary transitions.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `mouseout` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onmouseover

`onmouseover` handles `mouseover`. The mouse entered the target from another target; bubbling can include transitions involving descendants.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `mouseover` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onmouseup

`onmouseup` handles `mouseup`. A mouse button was released; a complete activation has additional rules.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `mouseup` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onoffline

`onoffline` handles `offline`. Window's environment reports an offline state; this is not an authoritative health check for a particular server.

Declared context: body. Prefer `offline` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### ononline

`ononline` handles `online`. Window's environment reports an online state; a reachable network interface does not guarantee the requested API works.

Declared context: body. Prefer `online` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onpagehide

`onpagehide` handles `pagehide`. A page is being hidden during navigation; persisted helps distinguish page-cache handling.

Declared context: body. Prefer `pagehide` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onpagereveal

`onpagereveal` handles `pagereveal`. A document is being revealed in the supported navigation-transition lifecycle; verify availability before relying on it.

Declared context: body. Prefer `pagereveal` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onpageshow

`onpageshow` handles `pageshow`. A page is shown, including relevant history-cache restoration; inspect persisted where needed.

Declared context: body. Prefer `pageshow` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onpageswap

`onpageswap` handles `pageswap`. A document is being swapped out in the supported navigation-transition lifecycle; this is not a persistence guarantee.

Declared context: body. Prefer `pageswap` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onpaste

`onpaste` handles `paste`. A paste operation is requested; treat clipboard content as external data and keep native behavior where appropriate.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `paste` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onpause

`onpause` handles `pause`. The media element entered its paused state through the defined transition.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `pause` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onplay

`onplay` handles `play`. The media element's paused state became false; this does not prove frames or audio are already advancing.

### onplaying

`onplaying` handles `playing`. Playback has begun or resumed after the relevant wait state.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `playing` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onpopstate

`onpopstate` handles `popstate`. The active history entry changed through a relevant session-history traversal; pushState itself does not fire it.

Declared context: body. Prefer `popstate` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onprogress

`onprogress` handles `progress`. Media resource fetching made progress under its event rules; do not confuse it with the progress element.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `progress` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onratechange

`onratechange` handles `ratechange`. The media playback rate changed; application controls should reflect the live value.

### onreset

`onreset` handles `reset`. A form reset was requested; cancellation and the reset algorithm determine resulting default states.

### onresize

`onresize` handles `resize`. The applicable target, commonly Window or media dimensions, changed size; this is not a generic element-size listener.

### onrejectionhandled

`onrejectionhandled` handles `rejectionhandled`. A previously unhandled promise rejection later acquired a rejection handler.

### onscroll

`onscroll` handles `scroll`. The relevant scroll position changed; use its actual target and avoid assuming every scroll is a user gesture.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `scroll` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onscrollend

`onscrollend` handles `scrollend`. A supported scrolling operation completed; browser availability and the specific scroller matter.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `scrollend` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onsecuritypolicyviolation

`onsecuritypolicyviolation` handles `securitypolicyviolation`. A relevant Content Security Policy violation was reported; inspect the policy and blocked resource context.

Declared context: HTML elements. Prefer `securitypolicyviolation` with addEventListener on the actual event target.

### onseeked

`onseeked` handles `seeked`. A media seek completed under the element's seek process.

### onseeking

`onseeking` handles `seeking`. A media seek began or is in progress under its defined state.

### onselect

`onselect` handles `select`. A supported text-control selection changed through the event's defined behavior; it is not the select element's value-change event.

### onslotchange

`onslotchange` handles `slotchange`. A slot's assigned-node list changed; arbitrary mutations within an already assigned descendant are different.

### onstalled

`onstalled` handles `stalled`. The media element is trying to fetch data but data is not arriving as expected.

`onstorage` handles `storage`. Another relevant document changed web storage; it is not a same-document mutation callback or a database transaction signal.

### onsubmit

`onsubmit` handles `submit`. A form reached its submit event through a valid path; SubmitEvent.submitter identifies the activating submitter when available.

### onsuspend

`onsuspend` handles `suspend`. The media element suspended resource fetching; this can be deliberate and need not mean failure.

### ontimeupdate

`ontimeupdate` handles `timeupdate`. The media playback position was updated; the event frequency is not a fixed animation clock.

### ontoggle

`ontoggle` handles `toggle`. A supported disclosure or popover state change is reported under its event processing rules.

### onunhandledrejection

`onunhandledrejection` handles `unhandledrejection`. A promise rejection currently lacks a handler; do not expose sensitive failure details in user-visible logs.

### Related event families from other specifications

The HTML handler index is not the complete universe of web events. Pointer Events adds pointerdown, pointerup, pointermove, pointerenter, pointerleave, pointerover, pointerout, pointercancel, gotpointercapture and lostpointercapture; current pointerrawupdate needs its own support check. Touch Events defines touchstart, touchmove, touchend and touchcancel. UI Events includes focusin, focusout, compositionstart, compositionupdate and compositionend. CSS animation and transition events and fullscreen/picture-in-picture events also have defining specifications. addEventListener can observe supported event types without requiring a core HTML on* attribute. Do not invent inline attributes merely because a string event name exists.
