## 8 How HTML attributes and Web APIs work together

### 8A The cooperation model

An element supplies meaning and a browser interface. Attributes configure a starting state or connect resources and nodes. Browser algorithms turn those declarations into behavior. Web APIs let code observe and change the resulting objects. Events signal relevant transitions. CSS renders states, and accessibility mappings expose supported semantics. A reliable interface keeps all these views aligned.

Consider input type=email required name=contact. HTML selects an email control; required adds a value constraint; name supplies the submission key. HTMLInputElement exposes value and validity. A form's submission algorithm checks interactive validity, then constructs entries. FormData exposes those entries to JavaScript. Fetch can send them to a server, which still validates them. No one attribute performs the whole workflow.

The useful question is always: who consumes this value? The parser consumes tag syntax; label association consumes an ID reference; the resource loader consumes src; the form algorithm consumes name and checkedness; assistive technology consumes accessibility mappings; an application's event handler consumes a click. Do not assume an attribute has an effect just because it is present.

### 8B Attributes reflected properties and live state

HTML attributes are strings, with absence represented by null from getAttribute. A boolean property can provide a convenient true or false interface to attribute presence. Some properties normalize or resolve the underlying value; others track independent live state.

```html
<label><input id="updates" type="checkbox" name="updates" checked>Updates</label>
<script>
const control = document.getElementById('updates');
console.log(control.getAttribute('checked')); // empty string initially
console.log(control.defaultChecked);         // true initially
control.checked = false;
console.log(control.hasAttribute('checked')); // still true
console.log(control.checked);                // false
control.disabled = true;                     // reflects presence
control.disabled = false;                    // removes disabled
</script>
```

The checked content attribute expresses a default. checked is live checkedness; defaultChecked reflects the default. Input value and defaultValue have their own dirty-value rules, so setting value does not generally rewrite the value attribute after interaction. Textarea starts from child text. Option selected and defaultSelected follow a comparable current/default distinction.

A URL property such as anchor.href can return an absolute resolved URL while getAttribute('href') retains authored relative text. dataset exposes strings rather than numbers or trusted values. classList manipulates tokens, and style is a CSS declaration object. These are several different reflection models, not one automatic attribute-to-property rule.

Practice: uncheck the example, reset its form in an extended fixture, and explain the resulting default and live states separately. Observe both getAttribute and the relevant properties. Do not use a MutationObserver on attributes to detect every live value change.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#dom-input-checked

### 8C Form validation entry construction and submission

Use HTML to describe control types, labels, constraints and submission names. Use validity APIs when a business rule needs additional client feedback. Keep the server responsible for authoritative validation, authentication and persistence.

```html
<form id="booking" action="/bookings" method="post">
  <label for="seats">Seats</label>
  <input id="seats" name="seats" type="number" min="1" max="8" required>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="updates" value="yes">Updates</label>
  <button type="submit" name="intent" value="reserve">Reserve</button>
</form>
<script>
const booking = document.getElementById('booking');
booking.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
  event.preventDefault(); // teaching inspection instead of a real booking
  const entries = new FormData(booking, event.submitter);
  console.log([...entries.entries()]);
});
</script>
```

The /bookings destination is an illustrative server contract, not a supplied backend. Normal user submission checks interactive validity before the submit event. A required empty seats field blocks that path. With seats=2 and updates unchecked, the expected relevant entries include seats=2 and intent=reserve, with no updates entry. Values are strings or File objects, not automatically numeric application values. Repeated names remain repeated; Object.fromEntries can lose repetitions.

form.checkValidity() reports validity through its defined checks and events, while reportValidity() requests interactive reporting. setCustomValidity('message') creates a custom error that must later be cleared with an empty string. requestSubmit(button) follows normal submitter and validation behavior; form.submit() bypasses interactive validation and the submit event. A control named submit can also shadow a form method, so use robust references and deliberate names.

When enhancing with Fetch, handle success and failure, keep useful status text, and prevent duplicate mutations at the server. If sending FormData, let the browser construct the multipart boundary rather than supplying a mismatched Content-Type manually. A GET native submission encodes entries into a query under its own algorithm; Fetch does not automatically reproduce a form's method, submitter overrides and navigation behavior merely because you pass it a form element.

Practice: compare unchecked, disabled and readonly controls; add two same-named checkboxes; activate two different submitters; inspect the real payload. For image submitters, test coordinate entries separately. Invalid user input is a learner result, while an unavailable receiver is infrastructure failure.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html
Source: https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-formdata
Source: https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/

### 8D Native dialogs dismissal and focus

The dialog element provides a browser interface with open, returnValue, show, showModal, close and current requestClose behavior. An open attribute alone shows a nonmodal dialog; showModal enters the modal workflow, including the browser's applicable background inertness and focus processing.

```html
<button id="review-open" type="button">Review booking</button>
<dialog id="review" aria-labelledby="review-heading">
  <h2 id="review-heading">Review booking</h2>
  <p>No reservation is sent by this example.</p>
  <form method="dialog">
    <button value="return" autofocus>Return to editing</button>
    <button value="confirm">Confirm review</button>
  </form>
</dialog>
<script>
const trigger = document.getElementById('review-open');
const review = document.getElementById('review');
trigger.addEventListener('click', () => review.showModal());
review.addEventListener('close', () => {
  console.log(review.returnValue);
});
</script>
```

The method=dialog form closes the dialog without making a booking network request. Its submitter's value supplies the return value. A real confirmation workflow must decide what that value authorizes and then perform the server operation separately. The cancel event concerns a close request; close reports a completed close. Do not infer that calling close and requestClose produce the same cancel path.

closedby selects user-dismissal behavior under current standard rules. Declarative commandfor plus command=show-modal can invoke a compatible dialog in implementations supporting the feature. Keep that newer declaration separate from the broadly understood method-based example, and test it in target engines.

Practice: open with keyboard, observe initial focus, move through the controls, attempt background interaction, request Escape dismissal, and close with each action. Check where focus returns, including when the trigger was removed. Do not replace the closing process by removing open and assume every event and cleanup step occurred.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-dialog-element
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-button-element

### 8E Popovers and disclosures

A details element with summary already has a disclosure interaction. Its open state is observable through the property and toggle event; name creates an exclusivity group under the current rules. Start there when the content is an inline answer.

```html
<button type="button" popovertarget="measuring-help">Measuring help</button>
<div id="measuring-help" popover>
  Measure the inside width in centimetres.
</div>
```

The target relationship connects the button and popover. The browser manages applicable showing and dismissal behavior; JavaScript can use showPopover, hidePopover and togglePopover when additional coordination is necessary. beforetoggle can expose an impending transition under its defined cancellation rules, and toggle reports a state change. Do not assume every close transition is cancelable.

Popover is not a complete application menu, tooltip or modal dialog. If the contents are a complex custom widget, its semantics, keyboard model and focus behavior still need design and testing. A title tooltip does not provide this interaction, and aria-expanded must not be treated as an implementation of hiding or revealing content.

Practice: compare an always-visible instruction, a details answer, an auto popover and a modal dialog for the same task. Explain which content must remain available before input, what dismisses each interaction, and whether the user can continue outside it. Check repeated activation and missing-feature fallback.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#the-details-element

### 8F Responsive images resource loading and canvas

img supplies the displayed image and alternative text. picture and source offer conditional candidates. srcset describes resource candidates, sizes describes source-size assumptions, and CSS determines the actual rendered space. The loader selects a resource using the relevant environment and selection algorithm; currentSrc exposes the chosen source.

```html
<img id="route-photo" src="route-640.jpg"
     srcset="route-640.jpg 640w, route-1280.jpg 1280w"
     sizes="(max-width: 40rem) 100vw, 40rem"
     width="1280" height="720"
     alt="A level boardwalk reaches the viewing platform">
<script>
const photo = document.getElementById('route-photo');
photo.addEventListener('load', () => {
  console.log(photo.currentSrc, photo.naturalWidth, photo.naturalHeight);
});
photo.addEventListener('error', () => {
  console.log('The photograph could not be loaded.');
});
</script>
```

The referenced images must be supplied by a later runnable exercise. The width and height declare an aspect ratio; they do not force the browser to request the 1280-pixel file. loading, decoding and fetchpriority guide different stages and are hints rather than timing promises. complete alone does not prove a successful usable image; inspect dimensions, load/error results and the relevant decode promise.

CanvasRenderingContext2D.drawImage can draw a loaded image into canvas. Reading pixels or exporting the canvas requires an origin-clean surface. A remote image without the right CORS handling can taint it; setting crossorigin does not make the remote server cooperate. Configure CORS before starting the request, and observe actual response headers.

Practice: change viewport and device scale, compare sizes to measured layout width, inspect currentSrc and network requests, and test a missing candidate. For a canvas extension use locally supplied images first, then a controlled cross-origin fixture. A screenshot alone cannot explain why a different candidate was chosen.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#security-with-canvas-elements

### 8G Media resources tracks and playback promises

Audio and video attributes configure source, buffering hints, initial mute state and controls. HTMLMediaElement exposes playback state, seeking, volume, duration, readyState and networkState. TextTrack interfaces expose timed tracks and cue changes. The source and track elements connect actual resources to those APIs.

```html
<video id="tour" controls width="640" height="360" preload="metadata">
  <source src="tour.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="tour-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
</video>
<button id="play-tour" type="button">Play tour</button>
<p id="play-status" role="status"></p>
<script>
const tour = document.getElementById('tour');
const status = document.getElementById('play-status');
document.getElementById('play-tour').addEventListener('click', async () => {
  try {
    await tour.play();
    status.textContent = 'The tour is playing.';
  } catch {
    status.textContent = 'Playback did not start. Try the video controls.';
  }
});
</script>
```

The sample requires a real local video and timed caption file. play returns a promise because playback can fail or be blocked. A click alone is not proof of success. loadedmetadata is the appropriate kind of transition for metadata-dependent work; canplay does not establish that the entire resource downloaded. Do not use timeupdate as a guaranteed fixed-rate timer.

Captions include relevant speech and non-speech sound; subtitles usually translate or transcribe dialogue; visual descriptions address information absent from the audio. Native controls do not generate these alternatives. Keep a transcript link outside the media element where it should remain available even in a supporting browser.

Practice: record load failure, blocked play, successful play, pause, seek and track selection. Inspect text-track mode rather than merely counting track elements. Test captions for content accuracy and timing manually; a valid WebVTT file can still be unusable.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html

### 8H Templates custom elements and Shadow DOM

Template content is inert reusable DOM held in template.content, a DocumentFragment. Cloning that fragment creates nodes that can be populated and inserted. This is a good place to connect semantic HTML with JavaScript data without concatenating untrusted HTML strings.

```html
<ul id="route-list"></ul>
<template id="route-template">
  <li><a></a></li>
</template>
<script>
const list = document.getElementById('route-list');
const template = document.getElementById('route-template');
const fragment = template.content.cloneNode(true);
const link = fragment.querySelector('a');
link.textContent = 'North boardwalk';
link.href = 'north.html';
list.append(fragment);
</script>
```

In this example the URL is a fixed author-controlled path. A dynamic URL would need a policy appropriate to its intended destination. cloneNode does not copy listeners added through addEventListener, and duplicating IDs creates broken associations; update IDs and references when cloning templates that contain them. Inserting the fragment moves its children into the list.

An autonomous custom element has a valid hyphenated name and a registered class. observedAttributes and attributeChangedCallback can react to chosen attribute changes; connectedCallback handles connection-dependent work. attachShadow creates a shadow root, and slot elements project selected light-DOM children. Declarative template shadowrootmode is consumed during the appropriate parsing path rather than by merely setting an attribute later.

Form-associated custom elements use ElementInternals and setFormValue to participate in form behavior; wrapping a div with a custom tag does not automatically submit a value. Labels, accessible relationships and focus must be reasoned about across the actual tree scopes. Newer registry, serialization, cloning and slot-assignment options need separate compatibility checks. A closed root is an encapsulation choice, not a hostile-code security boundary.

Practice: clone two entries with unique IDs, observe slotchange when projected children change, and compare an attribute callback to live property changes. Prefer a native control inside the component when it already provides the needed behavior.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#the-template-element
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html
Source: https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#shadow-trees

### 8I URLs navigation search and History

An anchor's href creates a native navigation path. target chooses the context, rel describes relevant relationships, and referrerpolicy affects request metadata. URL exposes structured parsing and resolution; URLSearchParams handles query parameters as entries rather than string concatenation.

```html
<a id="results" href="search.html">Open search results</a>
<script>
const results = document.getElementById('results');
const destination = new URL(results.getAttribute('href'), document.baseURI);
destination.searchParams.set('q', 'birds & bridges');
results.href = destination.href;
</script>
```

The ampersand belongs to one encoded parameter value. new URL performs parsing and resolution, not authorization. A base element can change fragment and relative-path resolution, so inspect document.baseURI before diagnosing a broken link. Do not use a disabled attribute on a link and expect native disabling.

History.pushState can update same-origin session history without fetching and rendering an entire new page. It does not update the page title, headings or focus by itself, and back navigation needs popstate handling in the application. A route represented only by a click handler often loses native sharing and fallback behavior unless deliberately implemented.

Practice: compare authored and resolved href values, introduce a base URL, and trace fragment navigation. For a client-routed extension, test direct entry to each URL, back/forward, modified clicks, error recovery and focus after the content update.

### 8J Events Fetch cancellation and status updates

EventTarget.addEventListener connects JavaScript to supported events without placing code strings in on* markup attributes. A click on a native button already has a keyboard activation path. A listener can then request data and update a real DOM region through textContent.

```html
<button id="load-note" type="button">Load visitor note</button>
<p id="note-status" role="status"></p>
<div id="note"></div>
<script>
let pending;
const trigger = document.getElementById('load-note');
const status = document.getElementById('note-status');
const note = document.getElementById('note');
trigger.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  pending?.abort();
  const request = new AbortController();
  pending = request;
  status.textContent = 'Loading visitor note.';
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/visitor-note.txt', { signal: request.signal });
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Request failed');
    const text = await response.text();
    if (pending !== request) return;
    note.textContent = text;
    status.textContent = 'Visitor note loaded.';
  } catch (error) {
    if (pending !== request || error.name === 'AbortError') return;
    status.textContent = 'The note could not be loaded. Try again.';
  }
});
</script>
```

A real fixture must supply the text endpoint. The request identity check prevents an older response from replacing newer content; cancellation alone is not a complete stale-response policy. Fetch resolves for HTTP error responses, so response.ok needs checking. AbortController cancels eligible client work; it does not roll back a completed server mutation.

The status region exists before updates and gives a nonurgent status cue without moving focus. Actual announcements still need assistive-technology testing. textContent renders text rather than interpreting markup. Neither an ARIA attribute nor a successful fetch proves that a user's intended operation completed correctly.

Practice: return a slow response, a quick newer response, an HTTP error and a network failure. Confirm the latest request controls the displayed text and status. Keep user focus stable unless the task requires an explicit navigation or dialog transition.

Source: https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-eventtarget
Source: https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-abortcontroller
Source: https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/

### 8K Observers files and drawing boundaries

MutationObserver reports configured DOM mutations, such as child-list changes or content-attribute changes. It is not a general listener for input.value, checkedness, layout or every accessibility transition. Use input and change for relevant user entry, ResizeObserver for observed size changes, and IntersectionObserver for intersection observations. These interfaces observe different facts and should not be used as interchangeable polling replacements.

A file input's files property exposes File objects selected by the user. File and Blob APIs read data asynchronously; accept does not make a file trustworthy. Drag-and-drop uses DragEvent and DataTransfer, and a drop target needs deliberate dragover handling. Keep the real labeled file input available so drag is an enhancement. Do not depend on assigning an arbitrary filesystem path to input.value.

Canvas width and height configure its bitmap coordinate space; CSS can scale the display separately. getContext obtains a rendering interface, and requestAnimationFrame coordinates animation with rendering opportunities rather than a fixed frame rate. Drawing a rectangle does not create a focusable button or text alternative. Keep essential chart data in an accessible DOM table and associate the canvas with a useful explanation.

Practice: explain why watching a value attribute misses a typed value, why a selected file can still be rejected by the receiver, and why a perfectly drawn chart needs a text representation. Record the specific observation rather than describing all three as a generic DOM test.

### 8L Security boundaries and the limits of declarations

HTML settings cooperate with HTTP policies, origins and permissions. iframe sandbox sets restrictions and selectively relaxes them through tokens. allow delegates eligible features within policy limits. A child document's contentWindow is a WindowProxy reference; it does not permit reading a cross-origin DOM. postMessage supports deliberate communication, with a precise target origin and validation of event.origin, event.source and payload shape.

CSP nonces authorize eligible inline code only under a real matching policy. Integrity validates eligible resource bytes but does not establish the resource's business correctness. crossorigin selects a request mode but does not change the remote server's policy. A hidden field or data-* attribute is client-controlled input. required and pattern help users correct data but never replace receiver validation.

Practice: trace the owner of each guarantee. The element declares intent; the browser enforces its implemented algorithm; HTTP policies and origins constrain capabilities; the server authorizes mutations; the instructor's runner isolates submissions. A reference document alone does not create those enforcement layers.

## 9 Curriculum levels and practice formats

### Common progression with different entry points

Use one set of mastery expectations for all learners. Beginners work through the foundations; switchers can demonstrate prerequisites and spend more time on changed mental models; interview learners can take the prerequisite checks before applying the interface skills to a DSA visualizer. This reading order does not impose a new subscription or progression policy on the application.

- Level 0 Document reading: explain tags versus elements, document structure, attributes, text escaping and the parsed DOM. Task: repair a small document shell and explain the first parser error.
- Level 1 Meaning and navigation: headings, landmarks, text semantics, lists, links and language. Task: build an article with a logical heading sequence and useful navigation labels.
- Level 2 Structured content and resources: tables, images, responsive selection, audio, video and embeds. Task: explain header associations and preserve meaning when a resource fails.
- Level 3 Input and submission: labels, field groups, all input states, constraints, entry lists and submitter behavior. Task: predict and then inspect a form payload for several control states.
- Level 4 State and native interaction: default versus live values, details, dialogs, popovers, focus and event handling. Task: diagnose a visually correct dialog whose actual open path is nonmodal.
- Level 5 Integration and robustness: templates, custom elements, Shadow DOM, fetch cancellation, origins and operational evidence. Task: build a small semantic interface with a working fallback and documented failure cases.

### Exercise formats with expected reasoning

Predict the DOM: provide a source fragment containing a p with a nested div. Expected reasoning identifies the parser's paragraph closure rather than claiming indentation controls parentage. Observe the actual tree in a browser before admitting a deterministic expected DOM fixture.

Predict the payload: provide named, unnamed, checked, unchecked, disabled and readonly controls with two submitters. Expected reasoning lists entries, repeated names and submitter contributions; values remain strings or files. It must distinguish input-image coordinate submission.

Trace state: begin with checked or value markup, simulate user changes, then reset the form. Expected reasoning separates defaults, live properties and attribute presence. Do not judge only from an HTML screenshot.

Choose the element: compare navigation, submission, inline explanation, modal confirmation, scalar measurement and task completion. Expected choices are a, submit control, details where suitable, dialog, meter and progress, with task-specific reasons and accepted alternatives.

Repair an association: break label.for, a table headers list, an image-map name or a popover target ID. Expected repair identifies the consumer and correct tree scope, not merely a similar-looking string.

Diagnose an async race: request a slow response followed by a newer fast response. Expected reasoning prevents stale results from replacing current content, handles abort and HTTP failure, and keeps useful status text.

Explain an accessibility limitation: provide a perfectly rendered canvas chart with no DOM alternative. Expected reasoning explains that pixels do not expose the chart's data relationships and supplies a meaningful adjacent representation.

Review a resource workflow: compare preload, media preload, lazy loading, decoding and fetchpriority. Expected reasoning identifies which stage each hint affects and refuses an unsupported exact timing promise.

### Seven integrated assignments

1. Semantic guide: create an article with header, navigation, main content, related aside and footer. Explain the heading hierarchy and language boundaries. Check fragment targets, DOM order and keyboard navigation.
2. Comparison table: present three learning plans with meaningful headers and a caption. Explain an interior value using its row and column labels. Include one deliberate span and justify it; accept a simpler table as a valid alternative when clearer.
3. Responsive gallery: supply local landscape and portrait images, alt decisions, dimensions and candidate lists. Measure layout and inspect currentSrc at controlled viewports; include a missing-resource case.
4. Registration workflow: build a labeled form with radio group, checkbox, textarea, numeric quantity and file input. Inspect payloads for empty, valid, excluded and multi-valued controls. The instructor supplies the receiver and server-side policy.
5. Help and review: use details for inline answers and dialog for review. Record open, cancel, close, focus and background interaction paths. Compare a popover only where the content is nonmodal.
6. Template directory: clone semantic entries, populate text safely, maintain unique IDs and keep links usable without client routing. Add a custom-element extension only after the native structure works.
7. DSA visualizer interface: describe a queue or set visualization with labeled controls, a textual state trace, a progress or status region and a semantic results table. The algorithm is implemented and tested separately in JavaScript. HTML success does not certify the algorithm, and an algorithm pass does not establish interface accessibility.

### Verification before a workout becomes authoritative

A runnable assignment needs actual source files, local assets, a declared HTML editing boundary, any read-only CSS or JavaScript, a deterministic receiver when needed, expected outcomes, accepted semantic alternatives and meaningful negative variants. Preserve the grader outside the learner's editable surface. Record exact browser and dependency versions, source hashes, commands, initial state and observed results.

Combine conformance checks, DOM relationships, network entry inspection and user interaction. Automated accessibility checks cover only part of the problem; review names, text alternatives, keyboard paths, zoom, focus and relevant assistive-technology behavior. Missing engines and unperformed manual checks remain untested. Never promote an example to a verified solution because a mentor explained it convincingly.

## 11 Legacy elements and integration boundaries

### Obsolete elements are migration knowledge

The following obsolete elements or legacy names can appear in older tutorials. They are not additional current HTML authoring elements and are excluded from the 113-element total. Their historical attributes are not part of the current conforming attribute dictionary. An old page must be inspected individually before choosing a replacement.

- acronym: older abbreviation markup; use abbr with an appropriate visible expansion.
- applet: Java applet embedding; replace the application workflow with supported web capabilities rather than mapping its attributes mechanically.
- basefont, font, big, center, strike and tt: presentational markup; use appropriate semantics and CSS. Use del only for a real deletion and s for inaccurate content.
- bgsound: background audio; use controlled audio with user choice.
- blink and marquee: legacy moving or blinking presentation; redesign the interaction and respect motion preferences.
- dir: legacy directory list; use ul for list semantics.
- frame, frameset and noframes: legacy frame documents; redesign navigation and use iframe only for a deliberate embedded document.
- isindex: legacy search prompt; use a labeled input and form.
- keygen: removed key-generation control; do not substitute an unrelated input and assume the old security workflow survives.
- listing, plaintext and xmp: legacy literal/preformatted parsing behavior; use pre and code with correct text escaping.
- menuitem: removed menu command element; use native buttons and an appropriate interaction pattern.
- multicol, nextid, nobr, spacer and image: historical or nonconforming names; use standard content, img where appropriate and CSS for layout or wrapping.
- noembed: legacy embedding fallback; use the supported resource element and an explicit useful alternative.
- param: formerly configured object resources; current object usage must not depend on removed plugin parameters.
- rb and rtc: older ruby structures not in the observed current HTML element index; use current ruby, rt and rp structures and check the actual writing-system requirement.
- content and shadow: older Shadow DOM projection names; use current slot and supported Shadow DOM APIs.

Legacy attributes such as align, bgcolor, border for presentational table layout, cellpadding, cellspacing, clear, frameborder, scrolling, language on script and type=text/javascript used as an unnecessary modern default should not be learned as a generic current attribute set. Not every legacy-looking spelling is obsolete: type=text/javascript remains an allowed script MIME declaration though usually unnecessary, and width/height retain specific current uses. Consult the obsolete-features chapter for the precise element and attribute pair before migrating it.

Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/obsolete.html

### Foreign content and noncore attribute families

SVG and MathML have separate namespaces and specialized parsing integration points inside HTML. Their svg and math roots are included in the specification's cross-technology index but are not HTML-namespace elements. viewBox, path data and MathML operators need their own references; copying the HTML global-attribute rules wholesale into those vocabularies is incorrect. In text/html, xmlns is not a switch that turns an arbitrary subtree into a different parser mode.

part and exportparts connect component internals to CSS Shadow Parts styling rules. Media extensions such as controlslist, disablepictureinpicture and disableremoteplayback, file capture attributes, and vendor-prefixed additions come from other specifications or implementations. They are not silently counted as core HTML attributes here. Read the defining specification and test support before adding them to a target-specific curriculum.

Autonomous custom elements use valid hyphenated names and can define their own attribute vocabulary. Define each custom attribute's grammar, default, property reflection and mutation behavior. Their attributes do not acquire native meaning by resemblance to disabled, required or value. A form-associated custom element must implement the relevant internals contract.

### ARIA attributes are a separate semantic vocabulary

role and aria-* supplement the browser's accessibility representation. HTML's allowed-role and attribute rules still apply; not every role allows every state, and some elements prohibit author naming. Prefer the native control and native state when available. An ARIA value of false is usually a literal state token, which differs from a boolean HTML attribute present with the string false.

Useful relationships include aria-labelledby for a name from ID references, aria-describedby for descriptions, aria-details for associated detailed content, aria-controls for a controlled region, aria-owns for an explicit accessibility ownership relationship, aria-activedescendant for a managed active item, and aria-errormessage for an error relationship used with valid error-state handling. A relationship alone does not move DOM nodes, focus a target or reveal a region.

Useful states include aria-expanded, aria-pressed, aria-selected, aria-checked, aria-disabled, aria-invalid, aria-busy and aria-current. They report different concepts. aria-disabled does not stop events; aria-hidden hides content from accessibility exposure without hiding it visually and must not create a focusable-but-unavailable interface. aria-required does not perform form validation.

Useful presentation and value properties include aria-label, aria-description, aria-roledescription, aria-live, aria-atomic, aria-relevant, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext, aria-orientation and aria-sort. A live-region role such as status supplies semantics, while actual announcement behavior needs testing. Sorting a DOM table and announcing a sort state are separate responsibilities.

This is an explanatory ARIA bridge, not a substitute for the complete role-specific ARIA reference. The HTML attribute inventory is exhaustive within its stated source; these external ARIA examples are intentionally selected. Use WAI-ARIA 1.2 and ARIA in HTML for a complete valid state/property set and per-element allowances.

Source: https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/
Source: https://www.w3.org/TR/html-aria/

Coverage is tied to the public specification pages retrieved on October 16 2026. The specification is living text, so the included inventory and source hashes record what was used. Some current features are newer than the original HTML5 snapshot and some browser implementations lag behind the standard. Specification coverage is not a browser compatibility certification. Newer features are called out where they need particular care.
SVG and MathML can be embedded in an HTML document but have their own element and attribute vocabularies. They are explained as integration boundaries rather than counted among the 113 HTML elements. Obsolete elements are listed in a migration appendix and are not presented as current authoring choices. Arbitrary data-* attributes and custom-element attributes are open-ended families; no finite list could exhaust every application's additions. ARIA, CSS Shadow Parts and media extension attributes are separately identified so their rules are not confused with core HTML.
This is tutor reference material with original examples and expected reasoning, not a package of admitted graded workouts. Illustrations that refer to images, servers or scripts need those resources before execution. The practice tasks state what should be observed; no browser run, screen-reader result or cross-browser pass is implied by the presence of example code. ### Reading routes
- New learner: read Part 2, document and text elements, shared attributes, then forms and resource elements. Work through the API examples after understanding the markup.
- Language switcher: focus on parsed DOM versus source, string attributes versus live properties, input applicability, native behavior, and browser security boundaries.
- Interview or DSA learner: use HTML as the interface layer for an algorithm visualizer or practice tool. HTML describes the interface; JavaScript or another executable language implements the algorithm. Do not invent a time complexity for a tag.
- Mentor or content author: retrieve the element entry, its attribute records, the relevant API case study and the misconception together. A fluent answer is not execution evidence.
## 2 Fourteen teaching lenses

13. Patterns: Which navigation, input, disclosure, media or component workflow uses the feature?

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · From source to behavior
### From source to behavior
HTML bytes are decoded, tokenized and parsed into a DOM tree. The tree is not a literal copy of tag indentation. The parser may close a paragraph before a div, insert a tbody, or otherwise recover from malformed source. Conformance and recovery are different: a browser displaying something does not prove the source is valid.
DOM nodes expose interfaces such as HTMLInputElement and HTMLDialogElement. Attributes are serialized settings, while interface properties can reflect settings, resolve URLs, expose live state or hold a value with no content-attribute counterpart. CSS uses the tree for styling and layout; accessibility mappings use its semantics and state; resource loaders and Web APIs use element-specific algorithms. A single change can affect several of these consumers.
A tag is syntax in the source. An element is the resulting structured object. A void element, such as img or input, has no HTML end tag. A slash on a void start tag does not switch the document to XML. A comment and a doctype are markup constructs rather than element tags. For a normal HTML document use <!doctype html> so the browser can select standards mode.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · Attribute value models
### Attribute value models
A boolean attribute is true by presence: disabled="false" still supplies disabled. Remove the attribute or set the corresponding boolean property to false when the intended state is off. Enumerated attributes, such as contenteditable and draggable, interpret defined keywords; their missing and invalid states can differ. Do not transfer a boolean rule to an enumerated attribute.
Token-list attributes such as class and rel contain separate tokens rather than arbitrary prose. URL attributes are resolved against the document base and may expose a normalized absolute URL through a property. Numeric attributes can clamp, default or reject invalid values according to their own rules. ID references connect nodes, so duplicates and incorrect tree scope can break a relationship even when the text looks right.
In text content, escape an actual markup less-than sign as < and an ampersand beginning a character reference as appropriate. Attribute quoting, URL validation, CSS strings and JavaScript strings are distinct contexts. Escaping a text node is not a universal sanitizer for a URL, script or iframe document.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · Evidence and accessible behavior
### Evidence and accessible behavior
Begin with a semantic choice: a navigates, button acts, table expresses data relationships, and label names a control. Native HTML can provide useful keyboard and state behavior with no script. ARIA supplements permitted semantics; it cannot make a div behave like a button or stop interaction merely by declaring aria-disabled.
Inspect authored source, parsed DOM, computed accessibility names, keyboard behavior and actual network requests as different kinds of evidence. For example, a form can look correct but omit a field from submission because name is missing or the control is disabled. An image can load while its alternative is misleading. A dialog can look modal while background interaction remains available because it was opened nonmodally.
References: WHATWG syntax, DOM, common DOM interfaces and interaction chapters; W3C ARIA in HTML. Exact topic links appear in the element and attribute records.
## 3 Shared attributes and their families
These attributes apply across HTML elements, subject to defined context and behavior. An attribute can be syntactically available while having no useful effect on a particular element. Event handlers are in Part 7; ARIA and other specifications are distinguished in Part 11. The same dictionary IDs are used throughout this document.
### A004 accesskey
`accesskey`. Suggest keyboard shortcuts using space-separated single-character tokens. The browser chooses the actual modifier combination.
Watch for: Shortcuts can conflict with browser or assistive-technology commands; never make them the only path.

### A010 aria-family
`aria-*`. Provide defined ARIA states, relationships and properties where allowed for the element or role.
Watch for: This is a separate finite vocabulary, not permission to invent arbitrary aria names or duplicate native state.
### A013 autocapitalize
`autocapitalize`. Recommend capitalization behavior for supported text-entry methods, with values such as sentences, words, characters, none or off.
Watch for: This is an input-method hint, not a transformation or validation rule.
### A015 autocorrect
`autocorrect`. Recommend whether supported entry methods correct user text, using on or off.
Watch for: Do not assume every browser or keyboard honors the preference.
### A016 autofocus
`autofocus`. Request focus during the applicable document or dialog focus process. It is a boolean attribute.
Watch for: Choose focus deliberately; unexpected focus can skip context or open an on-screen keyboard.
### A022 class
`class`. Assign space-separated class tokens used by selectors and application conventions. classList provides token operations.
Watch for: A class name has no native HTML meaning and does not grant a role.
### A031 contenteditable
`contenteditable`. Enable editing using true, false or plaintext-only; an empty value enables editing. Behavior can inherit from an ancestor.
Watch for: This is enumerated, not boolean; editable content still needs sanitization and storage logic.
### A036 data-family
`data-*`. Carry application-defined string data through valid custom data attribute names, such as data-route-id. dataset maps hyphenated names to DOMStringMap keys.
Watch for: The family is open-ended; it has no finite attribute list, and data is neither hidden nor trusted.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A041 dir
### A041 dir
`dir`. Specify ltr, rtl or auto text direction. bdo specifically needs an explicit ltr or rtl override.
Watch for: Direction is not the language, and right alignment is not a substitute for directionality.
### A045 draggable
`draggable`. Request drag behavior with true or false. Native auto behavior differs by element.
Watch for: It is enumerated; draggable="false" actually means false, unlike disabled="false".
### A047 enterkeyhint
`enterkeyhint`. Suggest an enter-key label or action such as search, send, next or done on supported virtual keyboards.
Watch for: It does not implement the action or change submission semantics.
### A057 headingoffset
`headingoffset`. Apply a numeric offset to descendant heading levels under the current heading-level rules; allowed values are 0 through 8.
Watch for: This is a newer standard feature; keep explicit meaningful heading ranks and test accessibility mappings before relying on it.
### A058 headingreset
`headingreset`. Stop heading-offset computation from continuing beyond the marked element. It is a boolean boundary.
Watch for: This does not rewrite heading tag names or establish tested browser support.
### A060 hidden
`hidden`. Mark content as currently irrelevant to presentation. hidden or empty represents the ordinary hidden state; until-found supports a distinct reveal workflow.
Watch for: hidden="false" is still hidden. CSS can affect rendering, and hidden content is not secret.
### A065 id
`id`. Give an element a unique nonempty identifier without ASCII whitespace in its tree. IDs support fragments, labels, scripts and ID references.
Watch for: Duplicates can silently redirect associations; window named properties are not a safe lookup strategy.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A068 inert
### A068 inert
`inert`. Make a subtree inert for applicable user interaction and focus behavior. It is boolean.
Watch for: It does not authorize access or remove source data; consider modal and flat-tree behavior.
### A069 inputmode
`inputmode`. Hint the entry modality using text, tel, email, url, numeric, decimal, search or none.
Watch for: A numeric keyboard hint accepts no validation responsibility and does not turn text into a number.
### A071 is
`is`. Request a defined customized built-in element at creation, using its registered custom-element name.
Watch for: Changing is later does not upgrade an ordinary element into the requested built-in; support needs checking.
### A073 itemid
`itemid`. Provide a global identifier for a microdata item where the vocabulary and item context allow it.
Watch for: An item ID is metadata, not the DOM id attribute or a security credential.
### A074 itemprop
`itemprop`. Attach one or more microdata property names to an element. The value is derived from the element-specific microdata rules.
Watch for: Do not assume every property takes its value from textContent.
### A075 itemref
`itemref`. Reference additional elements by ID for a microdata item's properties.
Watch for: Resolve IDs in the intended scope and avoid cycles or accidental unrelated properties.
### A076 itemscope
`itemscope`. Start a microdata item. This boolean changes the metadata grouping of descendant properties.
Watch for: It does not instantiate a JavaScript object or validate a vocabulary.
### A077 itemtype
`itemtype`. Declare microdata type URLs on an item.
Watch for: The vocabulary is separate from HTML; a declared type does not guarantee a rich search result.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A080 lang
### A080 lang
`lang`. Declare the human language using a BCP 47 language tag, with inheritance where applicable.
Watch for: It can help pronunciation and processing; it does not translate content.
### A095 nonce
`nonce`. Carry a server-generated cryptographic nonce authorized by an actual Content Security Policy.
Watch for: A nonce without a matching policy does nothing; do not reuse predictable values as a security design.
### A103 popover
`popover`. Create a popover state using auto, manual or hint, with empty meaning auto under current rules.
Watch for: Popover does not automatically supply menu semantics, a modal focus boundary or tooltip usability.
### A113 role
`role`. Declare permitted accessibility semantics from the applicable ARIA role vocabulary.
Watch for: A role does not implement keyboard behavior, and HTML restricts which overrides are allowed.
### A128 slot
`slot`. Assign a light-DOM node to a named slot in a shadow host; an empty name targets the default slot.
Watch for: This attribute and the slot element's name connect different sides of projection.
### A130 spellcheck
`spellcheck`. Recommend spelling and grammar checking using true or false, with an empty value treated under its enumerated rules.
Watch for: It does not enforce language correctness or reliably prevent remote processing by all input tools.
### A137 style
`style`. Supply CSS declarations on the element. The style DOM property exposes a declaration object.
Watch for: It changes presentation; it does not change the content model or sanitize a CSS string.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A138 tabindex
### A138 tabindex
`tabindex`. Control focusability and sequential focus ordering through an integer. Zero follows normal ordering; negative values remove ordinary sequential entry while permitting relevant focus behavior.
Watch for: Avoid positive ordering as a routine layout repair, and do not make hidden controls focusable.
### A140 title
`title`. Provide advisory text, or a context-specific expansion or stylesheet title. Some elements specialize its meaning.
Watch for: It is not a dependable substitute for a label, visible instructions or image alternatives.
### A141 translate
`translate`. Specify whether text and applicable attribute values should be translated, using yes or no; empty means yes.
Watch for: It is guidance for localization tooling, not an access or privacy control.
### A147 writingsuggestions
`writingsuggestions`. Recommend whether writing suggestions are offered using true or false and the defined empty-value behavior.
Watch for: It is separate from spellcheck, autocorrect and application-generated completions.

Each entry identifies the attribute spelling, its consumers, value model and practical limit. The contexts and value grammar summaries come from the observed WHATWG attribute index; the explanations are teaching prose. HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A049 for definition
### A049 for definition
`for`. On label, reference one labelable control ID. On output, list contributing control IDs. On current template update mechanisms, identify a same-tree marker or start ProcessingInstruction by its name.
Watch for: These meanings are distinct; do not copy the same ID-list grammar between contexts.
Context: label. Value grammar: ID*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#attr-label-for
Context: output. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens consisting of IDs*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-output-for
Context: template. Value grammar: Text.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#attr-template-for
### A050 form definition
`form`. Associate an eligible element with a form by the form's ID.
Watch for: Visual containment is not the same as form ownership, and shadow-root boundaries affect associations.
Context: button; fieldset; input; object; output; select; textarea; form-associated custom elements. Value grammar: ID*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fae-form
### A051 formaction definition
`formaction`. Override the form's destination for the activated submit button or applicable input submitter.
Watch for: It applies to the submitter context, not arbitrary buttons or input types.
Context: button; input. Value grammar: Valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-formaction

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A052 formenctype definition
### A052 formenctype definition
`formenctype`. Override the submission encoding for the activated applicable submitter.
Watch for: The override must be paired with a method and endpoint that can handle it.
Context: button; input. Value grammar: "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"; "multipart/form-data"; "text/plain".
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-formenctype
### A053 formmethod definition
`formmethod`. Override the form's get, post or dialog method through the applicable submitter.
Watch for: Dialog closes the dialog workflow rather than sending an ordinary network request.
Context: button; input. Value grammar: "get"; "post"; "dialog".
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-formmethod
### A054 formnovalidate definition
`formnovalidate`. Bypass interactive constraint validation for the applicable submitter. It is boolean.
Watch for: It never exempts the server from validating received data.
Context: button; input. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-formnovalidate
### A055 formtarget definition
`formtarget`. Override the navigation target for the applicable submission.
Watch for: Named contexts and special keywords are navigation choices, not authorization.
Context: button; input. Value grammar: Valid navigable target name or keyword.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-formtarget

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A056 headers definition
### A056 headers definition
`headers`. List the IDs of related th cells for a td or th.
Watch for: Each reference must identify the intended header in the table; arbitrary IDs do not define useful associations.
Context: td; th. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens consisting of IDs*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#attr-tdth-headers
### A057 headingoffset definition
`headingoffset`. Apply a numeric offset to descendant heading levels under the current heading-level rules; allowed values are 0 through 8.
Watch for: This is a newer standard feature; keep explicit meaningful heading ranks and test accessibility mappings before relying on it.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Valid non-negative integer between 0 and 8.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#attr-headingoffset
### A058 headingreset definition
`headingreset`. Stop heading-offset computation from continuing beyond the marked element. It is a boolean boundary.
Watch for: This does not rewrite heading tag names or establish tested browser support.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/sections.html#attr-headingreset
### A059 height definition
`height`. Set a vertical dimension on the eligible element. Canvas uses a backing-store coordinate dimension; image and video dimensions can reserve an aspect ratio.
Watch for: CSS display size and the underlying resource or bitmap size are different concepts.
Context: canvas; embed; iframe; img; input; object; source (in picture); video. Value grammar: Valid non-negative integer.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#attr-canvas-height

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A060 hidden definition
### A060 hidden definition
`hidden`. Mark content as currently irrelevant to presentation. hidden or empty represents the ordinary hidden state; until-found supports a distinct reveal workflow.
Watch for: hidden="false" is still hidden. CSS can affect rendering, and hidden content is not secret.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: "until-found"; "hidden"; the empty string.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#attr-hidden
### A061 high definition
`high`. On meter, set the beginning of the high-value subrange within the effective range.
Watch for: Thresholds must make sense alongside low, min, max and optimum.
Context: meter. Value grammar: Valid floating-point number*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-meter-high
### A062 href definition
`href`. Set a hyperlink destination on a or area, an external resource address on link, or the document base on base.
Watch for: The same spelling has different consumers; use document.baseURI and resolved DOM URLs when debugging.
Context: a; area. Value grammar: Valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#attr-hyperlink-href
Context: link. Value grammar: Valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-href
Context: base. Value grammar: Valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-base-href

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A063 hreflang definition
### A063 hreflang definition
`hreflang`. Hint the linked resource's human language using a valid language tag.
Watch for: It does not change this document's language or translate the destination.
Context: a; link. Value grammar: Valid BCP 47 language tag.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#attr-hyperlink-hreflang
### A064 http-equiv definition
`http-equiv`. Select a supported meta pragma, such as content-security-policy or refresh.
Watch for: It is not a universal way to set arbitrary HTTP response headers; several policies require real headers.
Context: meta. Value grammar: "content-type"; "default-style"; "refresh"; "x-ua-compatible"; "content-security-policy".
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-meta-http-equiv
### A065 id definition
`id`. Give an element a unique nonempty identifier without ASCII whitespace in its tree. IDs support fragments, labels, scripts and ID references.
Watch for: Duplicates can silently redirect associations; window named properties are not a safe lookup strategy.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Text*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#the-id-attribute
### A066 imagesizes definition
`imagesizes`. Describe source sizes for an image preload link using source-size syntax.
Watch for: Match the later responsive image's selection context to avoid unnecessary downloads.
Context: link. Value grammar: Valid source size list.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-imagesizes

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A067 imagesrcset definition
### A067 imagesrcset definition
`imagesrcset`. Offer image candidates for an image preload link.
Watch for: Use compatible candidate descriptors and pair its semantics with the later img request.
Context: link. Value grammar: Comma-separated list of image candidate strings.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-imagesrcset
### A068 inert definition
`inert`. Make a subtree inert for applicable user interaction and focus behavior. It is boolean.
Watch for: It does not authorize access or remove source data; consider modal and flat-tree behavior.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#the-inert-attribute
### A069 inputmode definition
`inputmode`. Hint the entry modality using text, tel, email, url, numeric, decimal, search or none.
Watch for: A numeric keyboard hint accepts no validation responsibility and does not turn text into a number.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: "none"; "text"; "tel"; "email"; "url"; "numeric"; "decimal"; "search".
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#attr-inputmode
### A070 integrity definition
`integrity`. Supply Subresource Integrity hashes for an eligible script or stylesheet resource.
Watch for: The hash must match exact served bytes; cross-origin checks also need the appropriate CORS response.
Context: link; script. Value grammar: Text.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-integrity

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A071 is definition
### A071 is definition
`is`. Request a defined customized built-in element at creation, using its registered custom-element name.
Watch for: Changing is later does not upgrade an ordinary element into the requested built-in; support needs checking.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Valid custom element name of a defined customized built-in element.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#attr-is
### A072 ismap definition
`ismap`. Declare an image as part of a server-side image map in its permitted anchor context.
Watch for: It is not the client-side usemap mechanism and still needs an understandable navigation alternative.
Context: img. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/embedded-content.html#attr-img-ismap
### A073 itemid definition
`itemid`. Provide a global identifier for a microdata item where the vocabulary and item context allow it.
Watch for: An item ID is metadata, not the DOM id attribute or a security credential.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/microdata.html#attr-itemid
### A074 itemprop definition
`itemprop`. Attach one or more microdata property names to an element. The value is derived from the element-specific microdata rules.
Watch for: Do not assume every property takes its value from textContent.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens consisting of valid absolute URLs, defined property names, or text*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/microdata.html#names:-the-itemprop-attribute

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A075 itemref definition
### A075 itemref definition
`itemref`. Reference additional elements by ID for a microdata item's properties.
Watch for: Resolve IDs in the intended scope and avoid cycles or accidental unrelated properties.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens consisting of IDs*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/microdata.html#attr-itemref
### A076 itemscope definition
`itemscope`. Start a microdata item. This boolean changes the metadata grouping of descendant properties.
Watch for: It does not instantiate a JavaScript object or validate a vocabulary.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/microdata.html#attr-itemscope
### A077 itemtype definition
`itemtype`. Declare microdata type URLs on an item.
Watch for: The vocabulary is separate from HTML; a declared type does not guarantee a rich search result.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens consisting of valid absolute URLs*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/microdata.html#attr-itemtype
### A078 kind definition
`kind`. Choose the text track category: subtitles, captions, descriptions, chapters or metadata.
Watch for: A kind keyword does not generate the necessary timed text.
Context: track. Value grammar: "subtitles"; "captions"; "descriptions"; "chapters"; "metadata".
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#attr-track-kind

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A079 label definition
### A079 label definition
`label`. Provide an optgroup's group label, an option's display label or a track's user-visible label.
Watch for: It is not the label element's for association.
Context: optgroup; option; track. Value grammar: Text.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-optgroup-label
### A080 lang definition
`lang`. Declare the human language using a BCP 47 language tag, with inheritance where applicable.
Watch for: It can help pronunciation and processing; it does not translate content.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Valid BCP 47 language tag or the empty string.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#attr-lang
### A081 list definition
`list`. Reference a datalist by ID for suggestions on applicable input states.
Watch for: It is not a closed-value constraint and is ignored on incompatible types.
Context: input. Value grammar: ID*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-list
### A082 loading definition
`loading`. Hint eager or lazy deferral for eligible img, iframe and, in the observed current standard, audio or video elements.
Watch for: This newer media application requires target testing; avoid delaying a resource essential to the initial task.
Context: iframe; img; audio; video. Value grammar: "lazy"; "eager".
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#attr-iframe-loading
### A083 loop definition
`loop`. Repeat media playback after completion where applicable. It is boolean.
Watch for: A loop can affect ended-event expectations and user control needs.
Context: audio; video. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#attr-media-loop

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A084 low definition
### A084 low definition
`low`. On meter, set the end of the low-value subrange.
Watch for: Interpret it with the full min, max, high and optimum configuration.
Context: meter. Value grammar: Valid floating-point number*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-meter-low
### A085 max definition
`max`. On applicable inputs, set an upper value bound in that type's grammar. On meter and progress, define a numeric upper range bound.
Watch for: A text input does not gain numeric range validation from max.
Context: input. Value grammar: Varies*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-max
Context: meter; progress. Value grammar: Valid floating-point number*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-meter-max
### A086 maxlength definition
`maxlength`. Limit text length for applicable input types and textarea under the platform's UTF-16 code-unit rules.
Watch for: It does not count user-perceived grapheme clusters and is not a server validation boundary.
Context: input; textarea. Value grammar: Valid non-negative integer.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-maxlength
### A087 media definition
`media`. Condition an eligible link, style, meta theme-color or source by a media query list in the applicable context.
Watch for: Do not assume the attribute has an effect for every meta name or source use.
Context: link; meta; source; style. Value grammar: Valid media query list.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-media

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A088 method definition
### A088 method definition
`method`. Choose form get, post or dialog behavior. Missing or invalid form method values use get under the normal rules.
Watch for: POST is not encryption; use HTTPS and validate on the server.
Context: form. Value grammar: "get"; "post"; "dialog".
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-method
### A089 min definition
`min`. On applicable inputs, set the lower bound in that type's grammar. On meter, define its lower numeric range bound.
Watch for: The type controls syntax, defaults and step-base behavior.
Context: input. Value grammar: Varies*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-min
Context: meter. Value grammar: Valid floating-point number*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-meter-min
### A090 minlength definition
`minlength`. Set a minimum applicable text length in UTF-16 code units.
Watch for: An optional empty field is not made required solely by minlength.
Context: input; textarea. Value grammar: Valid non-negative integer.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-minlength
### A091 multiple definition
`multiple`. Allow multiple values on select and applicable email or file input states.
Watch for: It does not create a multi-valued text or number input.
Context: input; select. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-multiple

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A092 muted definition
### A092 muted definition
`muted`. Set the default muted state of audio or video. The live muted property and defaultMuted need separate reasoning.
Watch for: The content attribute is a default, not a volume slider or a playback permission guarantee.
Context: audio; video. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#attr-media-muted
### A093 name definition
`name`. Identify a control's submission key or API name, a form, a browsing target, a map, a slot, metadata, or a details exclusivity group depending on the element.
Watch for: Names do not replace IDs; several same-named controls deliberately create repeated entries.
Context: button; fieldset; input; output; select; textarea; form-associated custom elements. Value grammar: Text*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fe-name
Context: details. Value grammar: Text*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#attr-details-name
Context: form. Value grammar: Text*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#attr-form-name
Context: iframe; object. Value grammar: Valid navigable target name or keyword.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/iframe-embed-object.html#attr-iframe-name
Context: map. Value grammar: Text*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/image-maps.html#attr-map-name
Context: meta. Value grammar: Text*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-meta-name
Context: slot. Value grammar: Text.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#attr-slot-name

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A094 nomodule definition
### A094 nomodule definition
`nomodule`. Skip a classic fallback script in environments supporting modules. It is boolean.
Watch for: This is not a declaration that the script itself is a module.
Context: script. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#attr-script-nomodule
### A095 nonce definition
`nonce`. Carry a server-generated cryptographic nonce authorized by an actual Content Security Policy.
Watch for: A nonce without a matching policy does nothing; do not reuse predictable values as a security design.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: Text.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/urls-and-fetching.html#attr-nonce
### A096 novalidate definition
`novalidate`. Bypass a form's interactive constraint-validation step during submission. It is boolean.
Watch for: Server validation remains required, and validity APIs still exist.
Context: form. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fs-novalidate
### A097 open definition
`open`. Set the expanded state of details or the showing state of dialog. It is boolean.
Watch for: Dialog open alone is nonmodal and does not reproduce showModal's workflow.
Context: details. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#attr-details-open
Context: dialog. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interactive-elements.html#attr-dialog-open

document:
HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A098 optimum definition
### A098 optimum definition
`optimum`. On meter, identify the best value so low and high subranges can be interpreted.
Watch for: A smaller value is not always worse; configure according to the measurement.
Context: meter. Value grammar: Valid floating-point number*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#attr-meter-optimum
### A099 pattern definition
`pattern`. Require an applicable nonempty input value to match the whole regular expression using current Unicode-aware v-flag rules.
Watch for: It has no / delimiters; empty optional values and incompatible input types need separate handling.
Context: input. Value grammar: Regular expression matching the JavaScript Pattern production.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-pattern
### A100 ping definition
`ping`. List space-separated URLs that can receive hyperlink-auditing notifications when a link is followed.
Watch for: It is a tracking-related network behavior subject to browser policy, not the destination link or a general Fetch API.
Context: a; area. Value grammar: Set of space-separated tokens consisting of valid non-empty URLs.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#ping
### A101 placeholder definition
`placeholder`. Supply a short entry hint inside compatible controls.
Watch for: It disappears during entry and must not be the only persistent label or instruction.
Context: input; textarea. Value grammar: Text*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-placeholder

document:
HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A102 playsinline definition
### A102 playsinline definition
`playsinline`. Encourage video playback within its element's area. It is boolean.
Watch for: It does not guarantee autoplay or override device policy.
Context: video. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#attr-video-playsinline
### A103 popover definition
`popover`. Create a popover state using auto, manual or hint, with empty meaning auto under current rules.
Watch for: Popover does not automatically supply menu semantics, a modal focus boundary or tooltip usability.
Context: HTML elements. Value grammar: "auto"; "manual"; "hint"; the empty string.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#attr-popover
### A104 popovertarget definition
`popovertarget`. Reference the ID of a popover target from an eligible button or input button control.
Watch for: The target must be a popover and the source must meet activation rules.
Context: button; input. Value grammar: ID*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#attr-popovertarget
### A105 popovertargetaction definition
`popovertargetaction`. Choose toggle, show or hide for the target popover.
Watch for: It does not create dialog modality or a complete menu keyboard model.
Context: button; input. Value grammar: "toggle"; "show"; "hide".
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/popover.html#attr-popovertargetaction
### A106 poster definition
`poster`. Set the video preview image URL.
Watch for: A poster does not replace the video's captions, transcript or source resources.
Context: video. Value grammar: Valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#attr-video-poster

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A107 preload definition
### A107 preload definition
`preload`. Hint none, metadata or auto media buffering, with the defined empty-value behavior.
Watch for: It differs from link rel=preload; browser policy can ignore the hint.
Context: audio; video. Value grammar: "none"; "metadata"; "auto"; the empty string.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/media.html#attr-media-preload
### A108 readonly definition
`readonly`. Prevent user edits on applicable textual controls while preserving relevant submission behavior.
Watch for: It does not apply to every input type and differs from disabled and aria-readonly.
Context: input; textarea. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-readonly
Context: form-associated custom elements. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#attr-face-readonly
### A109 referrerpolicy definition
`referrerpolicy`. Select which referrer information accompanies eligible requests.
Watch for: It is not the CORS policy and does not grant access to response data.
Context: a; area; iframe; img; link; script. Value grammar: Referrer policy.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#attr-hyperlink-referrerpolicy

document:
HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · A110 rel definition
### A110 rel definition
`rel`. Describe link relationships using permitted space-separated tokens; eligible form relationships have their own defined subset.
Watch for: Not every token is valid or meaningful on every element.
Context: a; area. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#attr-hyperlink-rel
Context: link. Value grammar: Unordered set of unique space-separated tokens*.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-link-rel
### A111 required definition
`required`. Require a value or selection in an applicable control. Radios have group rules and selects have placeholder-option rules.
Watch for: It does not require every checkbox in a same-named group unless each checkbox's own rule requests it.
Context: input; select; textarea. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#attr-input-required
### A112 reversed definition
`reversed`. Number an ordered list in descending order. It is boolean.
Watch for: It does not reverse the DOM order or change the user's reading sequence.
Context: ol. Value grammar: Boolean attribute.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/grouping-content.html#attr-ol-reversed
### A113 role definition
`role`. Declare permitted accessibility semantics from the applicable ARIA role vocabulary.
Watch for: A role does not implement keyboard behavior, and HTML restricts which overrides are allowed.
Context: only where permitted by ARIA in HTML; see Part 11.

## 5 Complete current element catalogue
All 113 current HTML element names have an entry below. The attributes line gives exact dictionary IDs for element-specific settings and important specialized shared attributes. Every entry also uses the shared families in Part 3. No additional element-specific attributes means exactly that; global attributes and applicable event-handler families remain available.
The content-model summary is a navigation aid, not the full normative model. An asterisk in a summary indicates context-dependent restrictions in the linked definition. Flow describes general document content; phrasing describes text-level content; transparent means to apply the surrounding model with the element's additional restrictions; script-supporting content refers to the permitted script/template mechanisms. Read the linked detailed definition before building a strict validator.
