HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · Document metadata
### Document metadata
#### Element html
`<html>`. The document root contains the head and body. Set the page language here so descendants inherit it; use direction separately when needed.
Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.
DOM interface: `HTMLHtmlElement`. Context summary: parents none*; children head*; body*.
```html
<html lang="en"> ... </html>
```
Common mistake: A missing language declaration is not repaired by a translated page title.
Practice: explain why `html` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.
Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#the-html-element
#### Element head
`<head>`. Collect document metadata rather than visible page structure. A normal standalone document needs a useful title and an early encoding declaration.
Attributes: shared attributes from Part 3; no additional element-specific attributes in this catalogue.
DOM interface: `HTMLHeadElement`. Context summary: parents html; children metadata content*.
```html
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Field notebook</title></head>
```
Common mistake: Putting visible headings here causes parsing surprises rather than creating a second header.
Practice: explain why `head` fits the example, choose a valid alternative for a different task, and identify one DOM or interaction observation that would distinguish correct behavior.

The type attribute selects one of the following 22 states. Unknown or missing type normally falls back to text. The input attribute list is a union of capabilities across states, not permission to use every attribute on every state. An input remains a void element regardless of type.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · Input type text
### Input type text
`type="text"`. Accepts single-line plain text with text-specific constraints.
Use minlength, maxlength, pattern and placeholder where useful; label remains persistent.
### Input type search
`type="search"`. Accepts a single-line search query.
Its search purpose can affect native presentation; results still require a submission or application workflow.
### Input type tel
`type="tel"`. Accepts a telephone string without a universal built-in telephone grammar.
Use an appropriate autocomplete token and visible format guidance rather than assuming all countries share a pattern.
### Input type url
`type="url"`. Accepts a URL with URL-state validation.
Syntax acceptance is not a safe allowlist for destinations and does not fetch the URL.
### Input type email
`type="email"`. Accepts an email string, or a comma-separated list with multiple.
The platform syntax check does not establish mailbox existence or ownership.
### Input type password
`type="password"`. Accepts a masked text string.
Use current-password or new-password autocomplete appropriately; masking is not encryption.
### Input type date
`type="date"`. Accepts a calendar date, serialized as year-month-day under the date grammar.
Display can be localized; do not parse the visible date format as if it were the value string.
### Input type month
`type="month"`. Accepts a year and month.
Min, max and step use month-state rules rather than day units.
### Input type week
`type="week"`. Accepts a week-year and week number in the defined week format.
Week years do not always match the calendar year of every included day.
### Input type time
`type="time"`. Accepts a time without an associated date or time zone.
Step is measured using time-state units; an optional seconds component changes precision.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · Input type datetime-local
### Input type datetime-local
`type="datetime-local"`. Accepts a local date and time without a time-zone offset.
An appointment system must separately decide the relevant zone and daylight-saving rules.
### Input type number
`type="number"`. Accepts a numeric quantity with number-state validation and stepping.
Use min, max and step for quantities; use text for identifiers whose leading zeros matter.
### Input type range
`type="range"`. Selects a numeric value within an effective range.
Defaults and clamping differ from number; add a label and an output if users need the exact current value.
### Input type color
`type="color"`. Selects a color; the current standard includes colorspace and alpha settings.
Serialization can vary with the configured space; newer color features need target-browser checks.
### Input type checkbox
`type="checkbox"`. Represents an independent checked state.
Only checked controls contribute normal entries; absent value commonly yields on. required applies to that checkbox.
### Input type radio
`type="radio"`. Selects one checked choice within its group.
Grouping depends on name, form ownership and tree rules; required operates through group constraints.
### Input type file
`type="file"`. Lets the user select files.
accept is a chooser hint; multiple permits several files. The value property cannot assign an arbitrary local file path.
### Input type submit
`type="submit"`. Activates form submission and can contribute its own name/value as the submitter.
formaction, formenctype, formmethod, formnovalidate and formtarget apply in this context.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · Input type image
### Input type image
`type="image"`. Submits through an image control and contributes activation coordinates under image-submit rules.
Provide alt and src; width and height describe the image. Its payload differs from an ordinary submit button.
### Input type reset
`type="reset"`. Resets eligible associated controls to their defaults.
Reset is not a save or clear-everything operation and can discard user edits unexpectedly.
### Input type button
`type="button"`. Creates a push button without an inherent submission action.
Use value for its visible label; application code or a permitted popover relationship supplies the intended action.

### State by state content attribute map
The following map transposes the specification summary into readable groups. It lists the input-specific content attributes evaluated by that summary. Common disabled, form, name and type settings and the shared attribute families remain separate. Value has state-specific modes. Conditional annotations retain the summary meaning; consult the defining type section for edge cases.
- Hidden: `autocomplete`, `dirname`.
- Text, Search: `autocomplete`, `dirname`, `list`, `maxlength`, `minlength`, `pattern`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `required`, `size`.
- Telephone, URL: `autocomplete`, `dirname`, `list`, `maxlength`, `minlength`, `pattern`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `required`, `size`.
- Email: `autocomplete`, `dirname`, `list`, `maxlength`, `minlength`, `multiple`, `pattern`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `required`, `size`.
- Password: `autocomplete`, `dirname`, `maxlength`, `minlength`, `pattern`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `required`, `size`.
- Date, Month, Week, Time: `autocomplete`, `list`, `max`, `min`, `readonly`, `required`, `step`.
- Local Date and Time: `autocomplete`, `list`, `max`, `min`, `readonly`, `required`, `step`.
- Number: `autocomplete`, `list`, `max`, `min`, `placeholder`, `readonly`, `required`, `step`.
- Range: `autocomplete`, `list`, `max`, `min`, `step`.
- Color: `alpha`, `autocomplete`, `colorspace`, `list`.
- Checkbox, Radio Button: `checked`, `required`.
- File Upload: `accept`, `multiple`, `required`.
- Submit Button: `dirname`, `formaction`, `formenctype`, `formmethod`, `formnovalidate`, `formtarget`, `popovertarget`, `popovertargetaction`.

### Applicability rules to learn together
- Pattern and text-length constraints apply to the compatible text-like states, not number, date, file or checkbox. A number field uses min, max and step rather than pattern.
- Readonly applies to text-like and supported date/time/number states, not to checkbox, radio, range, color, file or button states. Disabled is a different control state.
- Multiple applies to email and file input; select has its own multiple attribute. Required applies to supported value and selection states, not hidden, range, color or action buttons.
- Checked applies to checkbox and radio defaults. Accept applies to file. Alpha and colorspace apply to color. Alt, src, width and height apply to image submitters.
- Submitter overrides apply to submit and image input states. Popover targeting applies to an eligible button state rather than every input.
- List supplies suggestions only for compatible states. Text-selection APIs such as selectionStart and setSelectionRange also have a narrower applicability set than all inputs.
- Hidden input has special submission cases such as _charset_; radio names define groups, while a checkbox name is a submission key and does not create radio exclusivity.

## 7 Complete indexed HTML event handler attributes
The observed HTML index lists 89 handler attributes. Each on-prefixed content attribute holds a JavaScript handler body, not the name of a callback function by magic. Prefer addEventListener in scripts so behavior is separate from markup and compatible with a deliberate CSP. An IDL property such as onclick normally holds one handler; listeners added with addEventListener use separate listener registration.
Global availability does not mean an event fires on every element. Some events do not bubble, some are not cancelable, and body aliases several Window handlers. The HTML handler index is not the complete universe of web events. HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · 8A The cooperation model
### 8A The cooperation model
An element supplies meaning and a browser interface. Attributes configure a starting state or connect resources and nodes. Browser algorithms turn those declarations into behavior. Web APIs let code observe and change the resulting objects. Events signal relevant transitions. CSS renders states, and accessibility mappings expose supported semantics. A reliable interface keeps all these views aligned.
Consider input type=email required name=contact. HTML selects an email control; required adds a value constraint; name supplies the submission key. HTMLInputElement exposes value and validity. A form's submission algorithm checks interactive validity, then constructs entries. FormData exposes those entries to JavaScript. Fetch can send them to a server, which still validates them. No one attribute performs the whole workflow.
The useful question is always: who consumes this value? The parser consumes tag syntax; label association consumes an ID reference; the resource loader consumes src; the form algorithm consumes name and checkedness; assistive technology consumes accessibility mappings; an application's event handler consumes a click. Do not assume an attribute has an effect just because it is present.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · 8B Attributes reflected properties and live state
### 8B Attributes reflected properties and live state
HTML attributes are strings, with absence represented by null from getAttribute. A boolean property can provide a convenient true or false interface to attribute presence. Some properties normalize or resolve the underlying value; others track independent live state.
```html
<label><input id="updates" type="checkbox" name="updates" checked>Updates</label>
<script>
const control = document.getElementById('updates');
console.log(control.getAttribute('checked')); // empty string initially
console.log(control.defaultChecked);         // true initially
control.checked = false;
console.log(control.hasAttribute('checked')); // still true
console.log(control.checked);                // false
control.disabled = true;                     // reflects presence
control.disabled = false;                    // removes disabled
</script>
```
The checked content attribute expresses a default. checked is live checkedness; defaultChecked reflects the default. Input value and defaultValue have their own dirty-value rules, so setting value does not generally rewrite the value attribute after interaction. Textarea starts from child text. Option selected and defaultSelected follow a comparable current/default distinction.

The /bookings destination is an illustrative server contract, not a supplied backend. Normal user submission checks interactive validity before the submit event. A required empty seats field blocks that path. With seats=2 and updates unchecked, the expected relevant entries include seats=2 and intent=reserve, with no updates entry. Values are strings or File objects, not automatically numeric application values. Repeated names remain repeated; Object.fromEntries can lose repetitions.
form.checkValidity() reports validity through its defined checks and events, while reportValidity() requests interactive reporting. setCustomValidity('message') creates a custom error that must later be cleared with an empty string. requestSubmit(button) follows normal submitter and validation behavior; form.submit() bypasses interactive validation and the submit event. A control named submit can also shadow a form method, so use robust references and deliberate names.
When enhancing with Fetch, handle success and failure, keep useful status text, and prevent duplicate mutations at the server. If sending FormData, let the browser construct the multipart boundary rather than supplying a mismatched Content-Type manually. A GET native submission encodes entries into a query under its own algorithm; Fetch does not automatically reproduce a form's method, submitter overrides and navigation behavior merely because you pass it a form element.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · 8E Popovers and disclosures ### 8E Popovers and disclosures A details element with summary already has a disclosure interaction. Its open state is observable through the property and toggle event; name creates an exclusivity group under the current rules. Start there when the content is an inline answer. ```html
Measure the inside width in centimetres.
``` The target relationship connects the button and popover. The browser manages applicable showing and dismissal behavior; JavaScript can use showPopover, hidePopover and togglePopover when additional coordination is necessary. beforetoggle can expose an impending transition under its defined cancellation rules, and toggle reports a state change. Do not assume every close transition is cancelable. Popover is not a complete application menu, tooltip or modal dialog. If the contents are a complex custom widget, its semantics, keyboard model and focus behavior still need design and testing. A title tooltip does not provide this interaction, and aria-expanded must not be treated as an implementation of hiding or revealing content. Practice: compare an always-visible instruction, a details answer, an auto popover and a modal dialog for the same task. Explain which content must remain available before input, what dismisses each interaction, and whether the user can continue outside it. Check repeated activation and missing-feature fallback. An autonomous custom element has a valid hyphenated name and a registered class. observedAttributes and attributeChangedCallback can react to chosen attribute changes; connectedCallback handles connection-dependent work. attachShadow creates a shadow root, and slot elements project selected light-DOM children. document: HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · 8I URLs navigation search and History ### 8I URLs navigation search and History An anchor's href creates a native navigation path. target chooses the context, rel describes relevant relationships, and referrerpolicy affects request metadata. URL exposes structured parsing and resolution; URLSearchParams handles query parameters as entries rather than string concatenation. ```html Open search results ``` The ampersand belongs to one encoded parameter value. new URL performs parsing and resolution, not authorization. A base element can change fragment and relative-path resolution, so inspect document.baseURI before diagnosing a broken link. Do not use a disabled attribute on a link and expect native disabling. History.pushState can update same-origin session history without fetching and rendering an entire new page. It does not update the page title, headings or focus by itself, and back navigation needs popstate handling in the application. A route represented only by a click handler often loses native sharing and fallback behavior unless deliberately implemented. Practice: compare authored and resolved href values, introduce a base URL, and trace fragment navigation. For a client-routed extension, test direct entry to each URL, back/forward, modified clicks, error recovery and focus after the content update. Source: https://url.spec.whatwg.org/ Source: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/nav-history-apis.html

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · 8K Observers files and drawing boundaries
### 8K Observers files and drawing boundaries
MutationObserver reports configured DOM mutations, such as child-list changes or content-attribute changes. It is not a general listener for input.value, checkedness, layout or every accessibility transition. Use input and change for relevant user entry, ResizeObserver for observed size changes, and IntersectionObserver for intersection observations. These interfaces observe different facts and should not be used as interchangeable polling replacements.
A file input's files property exposes File objects selected by the user. File and Blob APIs read data asynchronously; accept does not make a file trustworthy. Drag-and-drop uses DragEvent and DataTransfer, and a drop target needs deliberate dragover handling. Keep the real labeled file input available so drag is an enhancement. Do not depend on assigning an arbitrary filesystem path to input.value.
Canvas width and height configure its bitmap coordinate space; CSS can scale the display separately. getContext obtains a rendering interface, and requestAnimationFrame coordinates animation with rendering opportunities rather than a fixed frame rate. Drawing a rectangle does not create a focusable button or text alternative. Keep essential chart data in an accessible DOM table and associate the canvas with a useful explanation.
Practice: explain why watching a value attribute misses a typed value, why a selected file can still be rejected by the receiver, and why a perfectly drawn chart needs a text representation. Record the specific observation rather than describing all three as a generic DOM test.

### 8L Security boundaries and the limits of declarations
HTML settings cooperate with HTTP policies, origins and permissions. iframe sandbox sets restrictions and selectively relaxes them through tokens. allow delegates eligible features within policy limits. A child document's contentWindow is a WindowProxy reference; it does not permit reading a cross-origin DOM. postMessage supports deliberate communication, with a precise target origin and validation of event.origin, event.source and payload shape.
CSP nonces authorize eligible inline code only under a real matching policy. Integrity validates eligible resource bytes but does not establish the resource's business correctness. crossorigin selects a request mode but does not change the remote server's policy. A hidden field or data-* attribute is client-controlled input. required and pattern help users correct data but never replace receiver validation.
Practice: trace the owner of each guarantee. The element declares intent; the browser enforces its implemented algorithm; HTTP policies and origins constrain capabilities; the server authorizes mutations; the instructor's runner isolates submissions. A reference document alone does not create those enforcement layers.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · Common progression with different entry points
### Common progression with different entry points
Use one set of mastery expectations for all learners. Beginners work through the foundations; switchers can demonstrate prerequisites and spend more time on changed mental models; interview learners can take the prerequisite checks before applying the interface skills to a DSA visualizer. This reading order does not impose a new subscription or progression policy on the application.
- Level 0 Document reading: explain tags versus elements, document structure, attributes, text escaping and the parsed DOM. Task: repair a small document shell and explain the first parser error.
- Level 1 Meaning and navigation: headings, landmarks, text semantics, lists, links and language. Task: build an article with a logical heading sequence and useful navigation labels.
- Level 2 Structured content and resources: tables, images, responsive selection, audio, video and embeds. Task: explain header associations and preserve meaning when a resource fails.
- Level 3 Input and submission: labels, field groups, all input states, constraints, entry lists and submitter behavior. Task: predict and then inspect a form payload for several control states.
- Level 4 State and native interaction: default versus live values, details, dialogs, popovers, focus and event handling. Task: diagnose a visually correct dialog whose actual open path is nonmodal.
- Level 5 Integration and robustness: templates, custom elements, Shadow DOM, fetch cancellation, origins and operational evidence. Task: build a small semantic interface with a working fallback and documented failure cases.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · Seven integrated assignments
### Seven integrated assignments
1. Semantic guide: create an article with header, navigation, main content, related aside and footer. Explain the heading hierarchy and language boundaries. Check fragment targets, DOM order and keyboard navigation.
2. Comparison table: present three learning plans with meaningful headers and a caption. Explain an interior value using its row and column labels. Include one deliberate span and justify it; accept a simpler table as a valid alternative when clearer.
3. Responsive gallery: supply local landscape and portrait images, alt decisions, dimensions and candidate lists. Measure layout and inspect currentSrc at controlled viewports; include a missing-resource case.
4. Registration workflow: build a labeled form with radio group, checkbox, textarea, numeric quantity and file input. Inspect payloads for empty, valid, excluded and multi-valued controls. The instructor supplies the receiver and server-side policy.
5. Help and review: use details for inline answers and dialog for review. Record open, cancel, close, focus and background interaction paths. Compare a popover only where the content is nonmodal.
6. Template directory: clone semantic entries, populate text safely, maintain unique IDs and keep links usable without client routing. Add a custom-element extension only after the native structure works.
7. DSA visualizer interface: describe a queue or set visualization with labeled controls, a textual state trace, a progress or status region and a semantic results table. The algorithm is implemented and tested separately in JavaScript. HTML success does not certify the algorithm, and an algorithm pass does not establish interface accessibility.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · Obsolete elements are migration knowledge
### Obsolete elements are migration knowledge
The following obsolete elements or legacy names can appear in older tutorials. They are not additional current HTML authoring elements and are excluded from the 113-element total. Their historical attributes are not part of the current conforming attribute dictionary. An old page must be inspected individually before choosing a replacement.
- acronym: older abbreviation markup; use abbr with an appropriate visible expansion.
- applet: Java applet embedding; replace the application workflow with supported web capabilities rather than mapping its attributes mechanically.
- basefont, font, big, center, strike and tt: presentational markup; use appropriate semantics and CSS. Use del only for a real deletion and s for inaccurate content.
- bgsound: background audio; use controlled audio with user choice.
- blink and marquee: legacy moving or blinking presentation; redesign the interaction and respect motion preferences.
- dir: legacy directory list; use ul for list semantics.
- frame, frameset and noframes: legacy frame documents; redesign navigation and use iframe only for a deliberate embedded document.
- isindex: legacy search prompt; use a labeled input and form.
- keygen: removed key-generation control; do not substitute an unrelated input and assume the old security workflow survives.
- listing, plaintext and xmp: legacy literal/preformatted parsing behavior; use pre and code with correct text escaping.
- menuitem: removed menu command element; use native buttons and an appropriate interaction pattern.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · Foreign content and noncore attribute families
### Foreign content and noncore attribute families
SVG and MathML have separate namespaces and specialized parsing integration points inside HTML. Their svg and math roots are included in the specification's cross-technology index but are not HTML-namespace elements. viewBox, path data and MathML operators need their own references; copying the HTML global-attribute rules wholesale into those vocabularies is incorrect. In text/html, xmlns is not a switch that turns an arbitrary subtree into a different parser mode.
part and exportparts connect component internals to CSS Shadow Parts styling rules. Media extensions such as controlslist, disablepictureinpicture and disableremoteplayback, file capture attributes, and vendor-prefixed additions come from other specifications or implementations. They are not silently counted as core HTML attributes here. Read the defining specification and test support before adding them to a target-specific curriculum.
Autonomous custom elements use valid hyphenated names and can define their own attribute vocabulary. Define each custom attribute's grammar, default, property reflection and mutation behavior. Their attributes do not acquire native meaning by resemblance to disabled, required or value. A form-associated custom element must implement the relevant internals contract.

HTML elements attributes and Web APIs · ARIA attributes are a separate semantic vocabulary
### ARIA attributes are a separate semantic vocabulary
role and aria-* supplement the browser's accessibility representation. HTML's allowed-role and attribute rules still apply; not every role allows every state, and some elements prohibit author naming. Prefer the native control and native state when available. An ARIA value of false is usually a literal state token, which differs from a boolean HTML attribute present with the string false.
Useful relationships include aria-labelledby for a name from ID references, aria-describedby for descriptions, aria-details for associated detailed content, aria-controls for a controlled region, aria-owns for an explicit accessibility ownership relationship, aria-activedescendant for a managed active item, and aria-errormessage for an error relationship used with valid error-state handling. A relationship alone does not move DOM nodes, focus a target or reveal a region.
Useful states include aria-expanded, aria-pressed, aria-selected, aria-checked, aria-disabled, aria-invalid, aria-busy and aria-current. They report different concepts. aria-disabled does not stop events; aria-hidden hides content from accessibility exposure without hiding it visually and must not create a focusable-but-unavailable interface. aria-required does not perform form validation.

## 12 Sources coverage and provenance
The public WHATWG HTML index and detailed element definitions were retrieved on October 16 2026. Attribute coverage merges the element index, detailed content-attribute lists and context rows in the attribute index, because summary tables can lag detailed definitions. The dictionary contains 147 distinct names or families. The index contributes 180 contextual definitions; repeated spellings such as type, for, value, name and sizes are intentionally explained by context. A fixed snapshot is not claimed for living URLs.
The 113 HTML element entries exclude the separate SVG and MathML roots and the open-ended autonomous custom-element category. All 89 indexed HTML event-handler attributes and all 22 input type states are included. The inventory records these counts mechanically and provides source links for audit. Newer standard features are included with compatibility qualifications rather than described as universally implemented.
This guide builds on the prior HTML tutor reference, the supplied Sets and Queues and Deques curriculum blueprints, and the supplied HTML UI-patterns reference. Their pedagogical organization informed the lenses, misconceptions and exercises. Their embedded instructions and unverified claims were not treated as source authority for HTML behavior.
Source links throughout the guide identify defining technical references. Examples and explanatory prose are original teaching material. Short technical identifiers, attribute keyword lists, interface names and content-model summaries are factual reference data from the standards. HTML text is maintained by WHATWG under its published licensing terms; W3C standards have their own published document licenses.

Purpose and use
HTML describes the meaning and structure of web content. This guide supplies teaching material for a programming tutor: explanations, original examples, mistakes to discuss, debugging methods, and practice prompts. It belongs beside JavaScript and other languages in a web-learning platform, but HTML practice needs browser and accessibility observations rather than DSA-style function-output tests.

The subject is the HTML Living Standard, often informally called HTML5. Primary source sections are identified with source IDs throughout; the source register records their URLs, classifications, versions, and observation date. This guide supplies teaching material for a programming tutor: explanations, original examples, mistakes to discuss, debugging methods, and practice prompts. HTML is a markup language rather than a general-purpose programming language. It belongs beside JavaScript and other languages in a web-learning platform, but HTML practice needs browser and accessibility observations rather than DSA-style function-output tests. This guide covers the complete requested topic inventory: documents, semantics, links, images, tables, forms, native interaction, media, embedding, accessibility, robustness, resource loading, and integrated projects. It is a substantial foundation and reference, not a reproduction of every element, API, algorithm, or browser implementation in the HTML standard. Topic order is for navigating this document, not an imposed application curriculum. The subject is the HTML Living Standard, often informally called HTML5. Primary source sections are identified with source IDs throughout; the source register records their URLs, classifications, versions, and observation date. Original examples are authored for this guide and have not been executed in a browser. Practice prompts are discussion or authoring briefs, not verified graded workouts. Browser builds, screen-reader combinations, and test results are not invented. The Word and Markdown editions contain the same instructional material. The Markdown edition is suitable for a reference-document upload workflow. It contains no hidden grader, private exercise answer key, or subscription policy. Indexing this material supplies retrieval context; it does not fine-tune a model or establish executable exercise admission. Navigation 1. HTML CSS and JavaScript responsibilities 2. Document structure and metadata 3. Syntax attributes and text escaping 4. Source markup parsed DOM and XML 5. Language and direction 6. URLs paths and fragments 7. Sections headings and landmarks 8. Text lists quotations and dates 9. Links buttons and navigation context 10. Image alternatives and image failures 11. Responsive images and dimensions 12. Accessible data tables 13. Form labels names and instructions 14. Input types and input states 15. Choice controls and grouped fields 16. Form ownership submission and encoding 17. Validation and error communication 18. Disclosures hidden content and inert regions 19. Dialogs and progressive enhancement 20. Popovers and feature boundaries 21. Audio video captions and transcripts 22. Iframes permissions and origin boundaries 23. Keyboard access accessible names and ARIA 24. Markup integrity editing and injection risks 25. Stylesheets scripts and resource loading 26. Global attributes and metadata limits 27. A practical HTML debugging method 28. Integrated practice briefs 29. Reference projects and evaluation boundaries 30. Sources versions and evidence status 1 HTML CSS and JavaScript responsibilities Meaning presentation and behavior HTML identifies content and native controls. CSS controls presentation and layout. JavaScript supplies application logic and scripted behavior where needed. The boundaries interact: a browser can provide useful behavior directly from HTML, while CSS and JavaScript can also damage a correctly chosen element's usability. Start by deciding what a piece of content or interaction means before deciding how it should look. Consider a catalog entry with a product name, descriptive text, a navigation destination, and an action. A heading describes the entry's topic. A paragraph explains it. An anchor identifies a destination. A button represents an action. A large font or pointer cursor does not supply those meanings on its own. Native controls are valuable because they carry defined semantics and interaction behavior; they do not remove the need for labels, useful wording, and testing. Small teaching example

Trail notebook

A pocket notebook for recording route observations.

Read notebook details
This fragment expresses content and intent. The button does not implement comparison storage by existing in markup; a real comparison feature needs application behavior. Its explicit type avoids accidentally treating it as a form submission control when the fragment is reused inside a form. Reasoning and debugging Ask what should happen when someone activates each control and whether that outcome is navigation, submission, or a local application action. Inspect the actual element and its accessible name, not only its appearance. Try keyboard interaction in the eventual running interface. A decorative wrapper may be a div; a destination or action needs a more deliberate choice. Practice prompts Diagnose a card where every interaction is a clickable paragraph. Which interactions have different purposes? Design the semantic structure of a workshop listing without adding styling or implementing its booking logic. Sources S07 sectioning elements S09A the a element S14 the button element S23 author conformance requirements. Normative meanings are distinct from this guide's pedagogical choice to begin with intent. 2 Document structure and metadata A small document with explicit structure For ordinary HTML pages, use a document shell that makes the intended structure easy to inspect. The doctype is a legacy-required preamble associated with standards-mode parsing/rendering behavior. The html element is the document root; head holds document metadata; body holds page content. A title names the document rather than substituting for a visible heading. Opening hours for Meadow Library

Opening hours

The reading room opens at nine.

This is an original explanatory example, not an executed project. Prefer an explicit shell for teaching even though HTML allows some tags to be omitted in defined circumstances. Optional syntax is not a reason to hide the document's conceptual structure from a beginner. Encoding and viewport boundaries The encoding declaration should be early; a meta encoding declaration must be serialized completely within the first 1024 bytes of the document. Transport-level encoding also matters. A viewport declaration helps specify mobile viewport behavior, but does not make the layout responsive by itself. Avoid declarations intended to prevent users from zooming. Detailed viewport behavior needs real device/browser evidence; the inspected CSS Viewport text is an editor's draft. Common mistakes and diagnosis A page title of “Home” may be unhelpful among many tabs. A visible heading placed in head is not valid metadata. Declaring UTF-8 does not repair bytes saved in another encoding. When text is corrupted, inspect the saved encoding and response headers as well as the document declaration. Compare the original source with the parsed document before deciding that a browser has ignored a tag. Practice prompts Predict which information names a browser tab and which names the visible page topic in a travel itinerary document. Repair a document shell with misplaced metadata while preserving its original article text. Sources S01 the DOCTYPE and optional tags S04 html head title and character encoding declarations S25 viewport meta. Viewport recommendations here are accessibility-oriented author guidance, not tested cross-browser results. 3 Syntax attributes and text escaping Elements and attributes An element can have a start tag, attributes, content, and usually an end tag. Attributes describe properties or relationships; they are not all interpreted the same way. Use quoted attribute values as a readability convention. A boolean attribute is true by its presence, not by parsing the English word inside its value. Removing a boolean attribute expresses false in markup.

Use <strong> for importance, not <b> as a substitute.

The menu lists tea & biscuits.

Void elements and escaping Elements such as img, input, meta, link, and br are void elements: they do not have ordinary element content or an HTML end tag. A slash at the end of a void start tag does not turn HTML into XML. Literal less-than signs and ampersands need attention because they participate in markup and character references. Escaping depends on context; escaping text is not the same problem as validating a URL or safely embedding script data. Mistakes worth explaining disabled="false" still supplies the disabled boolean attribute. A closing input tag does not create a useful input container. Comments are not private storage. A source example that teaches punctuation should display that punctuation as text rather than accidentally create an element. Prefer standard characters when direct UTF-8 text is suitable; character references are a serialization tool rather than a requirement to encode every non-ASCII character. Debugging method Inspect whether the issue is an attribute's presence, its allowed value, or parsing of surrounding markup. Validate the smallest failing fragment in a full document. State the context before suggesting an escaping fix. Practice prompts Predict the state of a checkbox carrying a boolean attribute with an unexpected string value. Repair a documentation paragraph that accidentally turns sample markup into live elements. Sources S01 elements attributes character references and comments S06 boolean attributes. Quoting every value and using explicit shells are optional author conventions in this guide. 4 Source markup parsed DOM and XML Why source and DOM can differ HTML source is serialized text. The DOM is the tree produced by parsing and subsequently changed by scripts. HTML's parser has defined error-recovery rules and can create implied structure. Consequently, seeing a tree in developer tools does not prove that the authored source was conforming. A browser can display a page while repairing invalid nesting.

Our studio offers:

Morning ceramics sessions

This intentionally problematic example asks whether a block-like container belongs inside that paragraph's content model. Inspect the parsed tree and validator messages instead of assuming that indentation controls parentage. Repairing the source means choosing an appropriate structure, not merely changing the closing tag's visual position. HTML is not XML with forgiving spelling HTML and XML resources use different parsing rules. MIME type and parser selection matter. XML requires well-formed serialization; HTML has its own rules for case handling, void elements, optional tags, and error recovery. A document that looks XML-like is not necessarily processed as XML. Do not infer processing mode from a trailing slash alone. Content models and implementation observations A content model describes permitted contents of an element. It is different from CSS display behavior. Changing display does not rewrite that content model. Similarly, a later JavaScript mutation can create a DOM structure that was not present in the original response. Separate “the parser produced this tree” from “the application modified this tree.” Debugging method Keep three observations separate: saved/served source, parsed DOM, and computed presentation. Reproduce without application scripts when appropriate. Record the document's content type. Use a validator to find the first structural error; later messages may be consequences of that initial mistake. Practice prompts Predict where a browser may close a paragraph around invalid nested content, then verify with a controlled DOM observation later. Repair a malformed article without relying on CSS to disguise its structure. Sources S02 parsing HTML documents and tree construction S05 XML syntax S01 content-model restrictions. This guide reports no executed parser observation for the example. 5 Language and direction Language is not the same as direction The lang attribute identifies human language; dir specifies text direction. An English page can contain a right-to-left quotation, and a right-to-left page can contain an address or code token written left to right. Choose each attribute for its own purpose. Language declarations help language-sensitive processing, including speech pronunciation, but do not translate text.

Messages from visitors

A greeting in French: Bonjour.

مرحبا بكم

Reasoning about boundaries Put an overriding language declaration on the smallest useful region whose language actually changes. Avoid assigning a language solely because a word is styled differently. Direction should follow the text's linguistic needs rather than a desired visual alignment. A right-aligned English paragraph is not automatically right-to-left content. For unknown-direction user text, automatic direction handling and isolation elements such as bdi can be relevant. Their suitability depends on the surrounding content and expected input. Directionality is easy to misunderstand if examples use only one script or if the author reads the page visually without inspecting its declared language. Common mistakes and debugging A page's translated title and body can disagree with an unchanged root language. A region can inherit a declaration unintentionally. Test mixed-language phrases, numbers, and punctuation instead of only isolated letters. Inspect effective ancestor declarations and conduct assistive-technology checks with recorded speech-language settings. Installed fonts and language voices affect observations and should not be guessed. Practice prompts Diagnose a bilingual event listing whose root language never changes when the displayed content changes. Mark up a mixed-language interview transcript with deliberate language and direction boundaries, then explain each boundary. Sources S03 lang xml:lang dir and bidirectional text semantics S21 Language of Page and Language of Parts. Region selection and debugging steps are pedagogical recommendations; no speech output was tested. 6 URLs paths and fragments A URL is interpreted in context Relative references are resolved against a base URL. A page's directory, an optional base element, and the actual served address can therefore change what a reference means. A fragment identifies a location or target within a resource. File-system paths and web URLs are different namespaces; a path that works from one local folder may fail when the page is served elsewhere.
Packing advice Easy routes

Packing advice

Carry water and a map.

Why alternatives matter Document-relative paths can be convenient for related pages in a portable folder tree. Root-relative paths depend on the site's root arrangement. Absolute URLs identify a particular location more explicitly but can reduce portability. A base element affects many relative references, so it is a significant document decision rather than a casual path repair. Debugging method Write down the actual document URL, intended target, authored reference, and resolved URL. Inspect network requests for broken resources. Check path case on the serving environment. For fragments, check that IDs are unique and that the target is meaningful and reachable. Distinguish a failed request from a successful request returning the wrong resource or content type. A local teaching fixture should keep navigation within explicitly approved fixture origins. That operational restriction belongs to the practice runner; it is not a property guaranteed by ordinary anchor markup. Practice prompts Predict how a sibling image path resolves when the same page is moved one directory deeper. Repair a small museum site's links without inserting machine-specific absolute file paths. Sources S10 URLs S04 the base element S09 following hyperlinks. The choice among relative-path styles is an optional project convention, not a universal standard requirement. 7 Sections headings and landmarks Choose a structure that describes the content A heading labels a topic. main identifies the page's dominant content; nav represents a navigation section. article is useful for a self-contained composition, section for a thematic section, and aside for tangential content. header and footer describe introductory or concluding material in context. A div remains appropriate when a neutral grouping is needed and a more specific semantic element would misdescribe the content.

Willow Community Archive

Collections

Oral history collection

Recording visits

Visits are available by appointment.

Archive enquiries are welcome.

Heading hierarchy is an explicit authoring decision Choose heading levels to express topic relationships. Do not select a heading rank just to obtain a font size, and do not claim that nesting sections automatically fixes arbitrary heading ranks for users. Look at the document's actual headings and meaningful reading sequence. Landmark exposure can depend on an element's context; every header is not automatically a page-wide banner. Debugging method Read only the headings, then only the navigation labels, then the full content in DOM order. Does each sequence make sense? Check whether repeated navigation regions have useful distinguishing names. Ask whether a section is a real topic or merely a styling wrapper. Compare an article's standalone meaning with the larger page's purpose. Practice prompts Diagnose a long newsletter whose heading ranks were chosen by visual size. Choose semantic groupings for a research summary with a main report and a related-reading aside; justify alternatives. Sources S07 sectioning elements and headings and outlines S08 main and div S22H heading organization S39 page regions. The outline-reading exercise is a teaching recommendation, not a browser-support claim. 8 Text lists quotations and dates Text elements communicate distinctions Use paragraphs for paragraphs and lists for genuine item collections. An ordered list communicates an order; an unordered list need not. A description list can express names and associated descriptions. blockquote and q identify quotations. code identifies code, while pre preserves preformatted text structure. The time element can carry a machine-readable datetime value alongside human-readable wording.

Bring these items:

  • A notebook
  • A reusable bottle

The workshop starts on 4 November 2026. 

let total = 0;
total += 3;
Meaning differs from appearance strong indicates importance and em emphasis; visual bolding and italics alone do not express those exact distinctions. Elements such as b and i have their own text-level meanings rather than serving as a substitute for every design choice. Use CSS for purely presentational styling. A line break is not a reliable substitute for a paragraph or list structure. Common mistakes and alternatives A sequence of br-separated items loses useful list structure. A code example with unescaped angle brackets may become live markup. Preformatted text can become difficult to use at narrow widths, so the supplied presentation needs attention without changing the target HTML skill. A displayed date and its datetime value must describe the same event; avoid inventing a time zone for a date-only event. Debugging method Ask what relationship a reader should infer. Inspect the serialized characters of code samples. Review the page without its decorative styling. Check dates against their intended precision rather than manufacturing a complete timestamp when only a calendar date is known. Practice prompts Compare a list of ranked finalists with a list of unrelated equipment items; explain the structural choice. Repair a glossary and a preformatted command example while preserving their original meaning. Sources S08 grouping content S09A text-level semantics including strong em code and time S06 date/time microsyntaxes. 9 Links buttons and navigation context Match the control to the intention An anchor with href identifies navigation; a button represents an action and has form-related behavior where applicable. A label should explain the destination or action in context. “More” repeated across unrelated cards can be less useful than names that identify their destinations. A control that looks disabled needs behavior consistent with its semantics; anchors do not acquire native button disabling from a disabled attribute. Read the visitor access guide
Types and context Explicit button types make ordinary intent clearer. The inspected current standard gives missing/invalid button type an Auto state with conditional submit behavior; “every missing type always submits in every context” is too broad. A reset control can discard user edits, so include it only when that outcome is useful and understood. Target and rel choices affect navigation context and relationships. download requests download behavior but is not a promise that every resource, origin, browser, or response will produce the same result. Opening a new context should be a deliberate user-experience choice, not a blanket convention for every link. Debugging method Inspect element type, href or type, form owner, accessible name, and actual activation result. Try keyboard activation instead of testing only pointer clicks. For a fragment link, check target existence. For a download, inspect the response and origin context before blaming the link text. Practice prompts Diagnose an event card that uses anchors with empty destinations for local actions. Repair a navigation list and a form toolbar while explaining which controls navigate, submit, or perform an application action. Sources S09A a element S09 hyperlinks downloading and link types S14 button type and submit-button conditions S22 visible naming guidance. No new-tab or download behavior was executed for these examples. 10 Image alternatives and image failures Describe purpose in context Alternative text depends on the image's role. An informative image needs an alternative that conveys relevant information. A decorative image generally uses an empty alt value so that its decoration need not be announced. An image used as a link or control needs a useful functional name. A complex chart may need a short alternative plus a nearby fuller explanation or data table. Alternatives that are not equivalent A filename is usually a poor substitute for contextual meaning. “Image of” rarely supplies the important information by itself. A caption does not automatically replace the need to decide what alt should convey, and title is not a dependable replacement for the image alternative. Avoid duplicating a large nearby paragraph word for word when it adds no useful information. Boundary conditions Include missing-image and failed-resource cases in later exercises. The role and context should still be intelligible if the resource is unavailable. The author must know whether an image communicates information that the surrounding text lacks. A rule that merely checks alt is present or nonempty cannot judge whether the alternative is appropriate. Debugging method Explain the page with the image hidden, then explain the image's function in one sentence. Inspect the control or link name if the image is interactive. Review multiple contexts: a photo used as decoration on one page could communicate critical location information on another. Practice prompts Compare the same botanical illustration used as decoration and as identification evidence. Write alternatives for a local transport diagram and explain when a separate text description is necessary. Sources S11 img alternative-text requirements S22I image-purpose decision tree S33 informative images S34 decorative images. The adequacy judgments here are contextual authoring guidance requiring human review. 11 Responsive images and dimensions Image selection and layout are related but different Width and height attributes can describe an image's intrinsic aspect ratio. srcset offers candidates; sizes supplies source-size information for width-descriptor selection. picture can provide alternative sources for art direction or format choices, while img remains the image element. The browser's resource selection is a process, not a guarantee that one named file will always be chosen in every environment. Explain the size claim The sizes description needs to match the space the layout actually gives the image. It is not a CSS width rule by itself. Distinguish a width-descriptor candidate list from a density-descriptor candidate list rather than combining incompatible assumptions. For art direction, explain why a different crop preserves the important content better on a narrow viewport. Loading and stability Space reservation can reduce disruptive movement while an image loads. loading is a scheduling hint, not a precise deadline or proof that no fetch will occur before a specific scroll position. Consider which images are central to the current page task before casually deferring every image. Debugging method Control viewport, device scale, cache state, local asset dimensions, and CSS scaffolding. Observe currentSrc, natural dimensions, rendered geometry, and requests. Test landscape and portrait assets and a controlled missing resource. Do not accept a screenshot match as the only correctness rule. Practice prompts Diagnose a responsive image whose declared source size differs substantially from its rendered space. Plan a gallery that preserves meaningful crops for different viewport shapes without requiring new CSS knowledge from an HTML learner. Sources S11 picture source img dimensions and loading S12 responsive images and image resource selection. Geometry and resource outcomes remain untested in this guide. 12 Accessible data tables Tables represent relationships in data Use a table when row and column relationships help interpret the information. Caption gives the table a useful identity. Header cells and scope can express straightforward row/column associations. A product grid used purely for visual placement is a different problem and should not be forced into tabular markup.
Weekend room availability
RoomSeats
Cedar12
Birch8
Simple and complex structures Spans describe cells that cover multiple rows or columns; they are not a convenient way to hide a poorly understood data model. More complex associations can need explicit header relationships. Before adding complexity, ask whether two simpler tables or a different explanation would help users understand the data better. What not to infer A bold first row is not necessarily a semantic header row. A visually empty corner cell still needs a considered role in the model. Browser display of overlapping or irregular cells does not establish conformance or accessible relationships. Automated role inspection cannot establish every assistive technology's experience of a complex table. Debugging method For an interior data cell, state the row and column labels needed to interpret its value. Check whether those relationships are present in markup. Inspect caption, header cells, scope, IDs and headers where used, and spans. Test navigation with an appropriate recorded assistive-technology setup. Keep presentation fixed when evaluating the HTML relationships. Practice prompts Diagnose a timetable where time labels were styled as headings but authored as ordinary data cells. Design a comparison of two membership options and explain whether spans help or obscure its relationships. Sources S13 table caption th scope headers and table model S22T irregular headers S35 tables with two headers. Layout recommendations are pedagogical; no table/AT combination was executed. 13 Form labels names and instructions Give controls understandable identities A label can associate with a labelable control using for and a matching ID, or by containing the control where permitted. id identifies an element for relationships; name identifies a submitted field entry. They are related design choices, not interchangeable attributes. A visible label helps users understand a field before, during, and after entry.

Use an address you check regularly.

Names descriptions and instructions The accessible name identifies the control; a description can provide additional instructions. Placeholder text is transient and should not be the only label. Required-format instructions should be available when users need them rather than appearing only after a failed submission. A tooltip alone is not a reliable instruction strategy. Alternatives and mistakes Explicit and implicit labeling can both be valid for suitable controls. Do not reject one solely because the reference author preferred the other. Duplicate IDs can break relationships unexpectedly. A label targeting an unrelated or non-labelable element does not create the intended association. Avoid placing unrelated interactive content inside a label and assuming it will activate the field in the same way as label text. Debugging method Inspect the control's labels, computed name, and described-by references. Click the visible label and test keyboard navigation in a later running fixture. Check that instructions remain understandable when the input contains text. Review consistency between visible wording and the name exposed to assistive technology. Practice prompts Diagnose a parcel form where placeholder text is the only field identification. Construct labels and supplementary instructions for a newsletter preference form, explaining the difference between IDs and submitted field names. Sources S15 label association rules S22 labeling controls S32 form instructions S24 accessible name/description computation. Manual usability observations are still required. 14 Input types and input states Choose constraints for actual data Input types describe different data and control states. Text, email, URL, number, date, password, search, and file inputs have different purposes and applicable attributes. Choose a type for the information, not solely for a desired keyboard or appearance. An identifier containing digits is not automatically a quantity suitable for a number input. States have different consequences required requests an applicable nonempty/selected condition; it does not mean a server can trust the value. disabled and readonly differ in interaction and submission, and readonly does not apply to every input type. Autocomplete tokens communicate the intended data purpose; they do not guarantee an identical autofill experience in every browser. Password masking is presentation, not encryption or secure storage. File selection introduces file objects and encoding considerations rather than turning a file path into trusted application data. Date and number UI presentation can differ by environment. Always distinguish an observed control interface from the standardized value and validity rules. Debugging method Name the data's meaning, allowed empty state, allowed range/format, and expected submission. Check type-specific applicability before adding constraints. Test boundaries that are relevant: a value just below a minimum, an incompatible step, empty data, and a permitted value. Avoid assuming a particular localized date display or virtual keyboard without evidence. Practice prompts Compare a six-digit delivery reference with a count of boxes. Explain why similar-looking digits may need different controls. Repair constraints on a small reservation form and justify which fields are optional, required, or read-only. Sources S16 input states and type-specific constraints S17 disabled controls and validation S32 instructions. The choice of real-world data examples is original teaching material, not a tested UI result. 15 Choice controls and grouped fields Express choices and their relationships Checkboxes can represent independent choices; radios can express one choice within a group. Shared radio grouping needs deliberate names and ownership. fieldset groups related controls and legend names the group. select represents a selection interface; textarea represents multiline plain-text entry. Choose based on the task and relationships rather than expecting CSS to supply missing structure.
Preferred contact method
Initial state and user state Separate initial markup defaults from the current state after interaction. A selected option and a checked control are not arbitrary decorative markers. Disabled options and groups also need context. Use an instruction or legend that makes the decision understandable rather than repeating generic labels such as “Option 1.” An unchecked checkbox does not normally contribute the same entry as a checked checkbox with a value. If the application needs a false value, that is a submission-design issue to handle explicitly, not evidence that the browser lost a visible control. A select label, option labels, and the submitted option value serve related but different purposes. Debugging method Test the group as a group: initial state, changed choice, keyboard behavior, and submitted result. Check for accidentally shared names across unrelated radio groups. Inspect the group name and each individual control's name. Keep the learner's editable task limited to HTML; supply any state-observation JavaScript read-only. Practice prompts Diagnose two unrelated radio questions that unexpectedly affect one another. Choose controls for dietary preferences and a single arrival slot, then explain the submission representation of each. Sources S16 checkbox and radio states S14 select textarea fieldset and legend S17 constructing the entry list S22 control labeling S40 grouped controls. 16 Form ownership submission and encoding A form connects controls to an operation The form owner and submitter matter. A control can be associated using form where supported, not only by visual position. A submit button can contribute its own name/value and can override selected submission settings. Method and encoding describe how the entry list is sent; they do not establish that the receiver is secure or correct.
The /fixtures/catalog destination is a hypothetical local fixture contract, not a supplied or executed endpoint in this guide. What is actually submitted Think in entries rather than a screenshot of fields. Ordinary disabled controls, unchecked checkboxes/radios, and controls without an applicable name are not simply submitted as visible empty boxes. The submitter and control type affect inclusion. HTML tutor reference · 1 HTML CSS and JavaScript responsibilities 1 HTML CSS and JavaScript responsibilities Meaning presentation and behavior HTML identifies content and native controls. CSS controls presentation and layout. JavaScript supplies application logic and scripted behavior where needed. The boundaries interact: a browser can provide useful behavior directly from HTML, while CSS and JavaScript can also damage a correctly chosen element's usability. Start by deciding what a piece of content or interaction means before deciding how it should look. Consider a catalog entry with a product name, descriptive text, a navigation destination, and an action. A heading describes the entry's topic. A paragraph explains it. An anchor identifies a destination. A button represents an action. A large font or pointer cursor does not supply those meanings on its own. Native controls are valuable because they carry defined semantics and interaction behavior; they do not remove the need for labels, useful wording, and testing. Small teaching example

Trail notebook

A pocket notebook for recording route observations.

Read notebook details
This fragment expresses content and intent. The button does not implement comparison storage by existing in markup; a real comparison feature needs application behavior. Its explicit type avoids accidentally treating it as a form submission control when the fragment is reused inside a form.

HTML tutor reference · 1 HTML CSS and JavaScript responsibilities (continued)
Reasoning and debugging
Ask what should happen when someone activates each control and whether that outcome is navigation, submission, or a local application action. Inspect the actual element and its accessible name, not only its appearance. Try keyboard interaction in the eventual running interface. A decorative wrapper may be a div; a destination or action needs a more deliberate choice.
Practice prompts
Diagnose a card where every interaction is a clickable paragraph. Which interactions have different purposes?
Design the semantic structure of a workshop listing without adding styling or implementing its booking logic.
Sources S07 sectioning elements S09A the a element S14 the button element S23 author conformance requirements. Normative meanings are distinct from this guide's pedagogical choice to begin with intent.

HTML tutor reference · 2 Document structure and metadata 2 Document structure and metadata A small document with explicit structure For ordinary HTML pages, use a document shell that makes the intended structure easy to inspect. The doctype is a legacy-required preamble associated with standards-mode parsing/rendering behavior. The html element is the document root; head holds document metadata; body holds page content. A title names the document rather than substituting for a visible heading. Opening hours for Meadow Library

Opening hours

The reading room opens at nine.

This is an original explanatory example, not an executed project. Prefer an explicit shell for teaching even though HTML allows some tags to be omitted in defined circumstances. Optional syntax is not a reason to hide the document's conceptual structure from a beginner. Encoding and viewport boundaries The encoding declaration should be early; a meta encoding declaration must be serialized completely within the first 1024 bytes of the document. Transport-level encoding also matters. A viewport declaration helps specify mobile viewport behavior, but does not make the layout responsive by itself. Avoid declarations intended to prevent users from zooming. Detailed viewport behavior needs real device/browser evidence; the inspected CSS Viewport text is an editor's draft.

HTML tutor reference · 2 Document structure and metadata (continued)
Common mistakes and diagnosis
A page title of “Home” may be unhelpful among many tabs. A visible heading placed in head is not valid metadata. Declaring UTF-8 does not repair bytes saved in another encoding. When text is corrupted, inspect the saved encoding and response headers as well as the document declaration. Compare the original source with the parsed document before deciding that a browser has ignored a tag.
Practice prompts
Predict which information names a browser tab and which names the visible page topic in a travel itinerary document.
Repair a document shell with misplaced metadata while preserving its original article text.
Sources S01 the DOCTYPE and optional tags S04 html head title and character encoding declarations S25 viewport meta. Viewport recommendations here are accessibility-oriented author guidance, not tested cross-browser results.

HTML tutor reference · 3 Syntax attributes and text escaping 3 Syntax attributes and text escaping Elements and attributes An element can have a start tag, attributes, content, and usually an end tag. Attributes describe properties or relationships; they are not all interpreted the same way. Use quoted attribute values as a readability convention. A boolean attribute is true by its presence, not by parsing the English word inside its value. Removing a boolean attribute expresses false in markup.

Use <strong> for importance, not <b> as a substitute.

The menu lists tea & biscuits.

Void elements and escaping Elements such as img, input, meta, link, and br are void elements: they do not have ordinary element content or an HTML end tag. A slash at the end of a void start tag does not turn HTML into XML. Literal less-than signs and ampersands need attention because they participate in markup and character references. Escaping depends on context; escaping text is not the same problem as validating a URL or safely embedding script data. Mistakes worth explaining disabled="false" still supplies the disabled boolean attribute. A closing input tag does not create a useful input container. Comments are not private storage. A source example that teaches punctuation should display that punctuation as text rather than accidentally create an element. Prefer standard characters when direct UTF-8 text is suitable; character references are a serialization tool rather than a requirement to encode every non-ASCII character.

HTML tutor reference · 3 Syntax attributes and text escaping (continued)
Debugging method
Inspect whether the issue is an attribute's presence, its allowed value, or parsing of surrounding markup. Validate the smallest failing fragment in a full document. State the context before suggesting an escaping fix.
Practice prompts
Predict the state of a checkbox carrying a boolean attribute with an unexpected string value.
Repair a documentation paragraph that accidentally turns sample markup into live elements.
Sources S01 elements attributes character references and comments S06 boolean attributes. Quoting every value and using explicit shells are optional author conventions in this guide.

HTML tutor reference · 4 Source markup parsed DOM and XML 4 Source markup parsed DOM and XML Why source and DOM can differ HTML source is serialized text. The DOM is the tree produced by parsing and subsequently changed by scripts. HTML's parser has defined error-recovery rules and can create implied structure. Consequently, seeing a tree in developer tools does not prove that the authored source was conforming. A browser can display a page while repairing invalid nesting.

Our studio offers:

Morning ceramics sessions

This intentionally problematic example asks whether a block-like container belongs inside that paragraph's content model. Inspect the parsed tree and validator messages instead of assuming that indentation controls parentage. Repairing the source means choosing an appropriate structure, not merely changing the closing tag's visual position. HTML is not XML with forgiving spelling HTML and XML resources use different parsing rules. MIME type and parser selection matter. XML requires well-formed serialization; HTML has its own rules for case handling, void elements, optional tags, and error recovery. A document that looks XML-like is not necessarily processed as XML. Do not infer processing mode from a trailing slash alone.

HTML tutor reference · 4 Source markup parsed DOM and XML (continued)
Content models and implementation observations
A content model describes permitted contents of an element. It is different from CSS display behavior. Changing display does not rewrite that content model. Similarly, a later JavaScript mutation can create a DOM structure that was not present in the original response. Separate “the parser produced this tree” from “the application modified this tree.”
Debugging method
Keep three observations separate: saved/served source, parsed DOM, and computed presentation. Reproduce without application scripts when appropriate. Record the document's content type. Use a validator to find the first structural error; later messages may be consequences of that initial mistake.
Practice prompts
Predict where a browser may close a paragraph around invalid nested content, then verify with a controlled DOM observation later.
Repair a malformed article without relying on CSS to disguise its structure.
Sources S02 parsing HTML documents and tree construction S05 XML syntax S01 content-model restrictions. This guide reports no executed parser observation for the example.

HTML tutor reference · 5 Language and direction 5 Language and direction Language is not the same as direction The lang attribute identifies human language; dir specifies text direction. An English page can contain a right-to-left quotation, and a right-to-left page can contain an address or code token written left to right. Choose each attribute for its own purpose. Language declarations help language-sensitive processing, including speech pronunciation, but do not translate text.

Messages from visitors

A greeting in French: Bonjour.

مرحبا بكم

Reasoning about boundaries Put an overriding language declaration on the smallest useful region whose language actually changes. Avoid assigning a language solely because a word is styled differently. Direction should follow the text's linguistic needs rather than a desired visual alignment. A right-aligned English paragraph is not automatically right-to-left content. For unknown-direction user text, automatic direction handling and isolation elements such as bdi can be relevant. Their suitability depends on the surrounding content and expected input. Directionality is easy to misunderstand if examples use only one script or if the author reads the page visually without inspecting its declared language. Common mistakes and debugging A page's translated title and body can disagree with an unchanged root language. A region can inherit a declaration unintentionally. Test mixed-language phrases, numbers, and punctuation instead of only isolated letters. Inspect effective ancestor declarations and conduct assistive-technology checks with recorded speech-language settings. Installed fonts and language voices affect observations and should not be guessed.

HTML tutor reference · 5 Language and direction (continued)
Practice prompts
Diagnose a bilingual event listing whose root language never changes when the displayed content changes.
Mark up a mixed-language interview transcript with deliberate language and direction boundaries, then explain each boundary.
Sources S03 lang xml:lang dir and bidirectional text semantics S21 Language of Page and Language of Parts. Region selection and debugging steps are pedagogical recommendations; no speech output was tested.

HTML tutor reference · 6 URLs paths and fragments 6 URLs paths and fragments A URL is interpreted in context Relative references are resolved against a base URL. A page's directory, an optional base element, and the actual served address can therefore change what a reference means. A fragment identifies a location or target within a resource. File-system paths and web URLs are different namespaces; a path that works from one local folder may fail when the page is served elsewhere.
Packing advice Easy routes

Packing advice

Carry water and a map.

Why alternatives matter Document-relative paths can be convenient for related pages in a portable folder tree. Root-relative paths depend on the site's root arrangement. Absolute URLs identify a particular location more explicitly but can reduce portability. A base element affects many relative references, so it is a significant document decision rather than a casual path repair. Debugging method Write down the actual document URL, intended target, authored reference, and resolved URL. Inspect network requests for broken resources. Check path case on the serving environment. For fragments, check that IDs are unique and that the target is meaningful and reachable. Distinguish a failed request from a successful request returning the wrong resource or content type. A local teaching fixture should keep navigation within explicitly approved fixture origins. That operational restriction belongs to the practice runner; it is not a property guaranteed by ordinary anchor markup.

HTML tutor reference · 6 URLs paths and fragments (continued)
Practice prompts
Predict how a sibling image path resolves when the same page is moved one directory deeper.
Repair a small museum site's links without inserting machine-specific absolute file paths.
Sources S10 URLs S04 the base element S09 following hyperlinks. The choice among relative-path styles is an optional project convention, not a universal standard requirement.

HTML tutor reference · 7 Sections headings and landmarks 7 Sections headings and landmarks Choose a structure that describes the content A heading labels a topic. main identifies the page's dominant content; nav represents a navigation section. article is useful for a self-contained composition, section for a thematic section, and aside for tangential content. header and footer describe introductory or concluding material in context. A div remains appropriate when a neutral grouping is needed and a more specific semantic element would misdescribe the content.

Heading hierarchy is an explicit authoring decision Choose heading levels to express topic relationships. Do not select a heading rank just to obtain a font size, and do not claim that nesting sections automatically fixes arbitrary heading ranks for users. Look at the document's actual headings and meaningful reading sequence. Landmark exposure can depend on an element's context; every header is not automatically a page-wide banner. Debugging method Read only the headings, then only the navigation labels, then the full content in DOM order. Does each sequence make sense? Check whether repeated navigation regions have useful distinguishing names. Ask whether a section is a real topic or merely a styling wrapper. Compare an article's standalone meaning with the larger page's purpose.

HTML tutor reference · 7 Sections headings and landmarks (continued)
Practice prompts
Diagnose a long newsletter whose heading ranks were chosen by visual size.
Choose semantic groupings for a research summary with a main report and a related-reading aside; justify alternatives.
